title: A 1000-hour EEG-EMG-audio dataset of Japanese speech production
authors: Motoshige Sato; Ilya Horiguchi; Masakazu Inoue; Kenichi Tomeoka; Eri Hatakeyama; Yuya Kita; Atsushi Yamamoto; Ippei Fujisawa; Shuntaro Sasai
summary: A 1020-hour EEG-EMG-audio dataset of Japanese overt speech from three participants, with signal-quality and physiological validation but no decoding benchmarks.
sensor: 128/62/63-channel scalp EEG, 3-channel facial EMG, microphone
speaker: Not stated
key_result: Not reported
limitations: Only three Japanese male participants; evaluation limited to signal-quality checks without downstream decoding experiments.

title: A cross-species neural foundation model for end-to-end speech decoding
authors: Yizi Zhang; Linyang He; Chaofei Fan; Tingkai Liu; Han Yu; Trung Le; Jingyuan Li; Scott Linderman; Lea Duncker; Francis R. Willett; Nima Mesgarani; Liam Paninski
summary: Cascaded decoding with the pretrained encoder is a strong standard result; the end-to-end audio-LLM path beats the prior end-to-end entry but trails RNN cascades, and the cross-species gain is small.
sensor: Intracortical Utah arrays in ventral motor cortex (128 electrodes for T12, 256 for T15); thresholded spikes and spike-band power
task: Sentence decoding from attempted speech (Brain-to-Text '24 and '25 holdouts) and imagined speech (50-word set)
vocabulary: Large-vocabulary attempted-speech sentences; 50 words for imagined speech
speaker: Two participants (T12, T15); pretraining also on other human and monkey recordings
session: T12: 25 sessions over four months; T15: 45 sessions over 20 months
key_result: Cascaded decoding with the pretrained encoder reaches 6.35% (Brain-to-Text '24) and 4.06% ('25) holdout WER as single models, below every non-ensembled entry, and 5.10% and 1.76% with LLM-merged ensembles. The single end-to-end audio-LLM model reaches 15.67% and 11.06%: better than the prior end-to-end entry (24.69%) but behind the RNN baselines (9.76%, 6.67%); the headline 24.69% to 10.22% uses a 10-model ensemble.
limitations: Cross-species gain is small (validation PER 15.95% to 14.39% and 7.61% to 7.12%, one value per cell without seeds); pretraining can include the benchmark holdout recordings, and removing the fine-tuning participants' data from pretraining raises cascaded WER to 7.24% and 4.36%; ablations report no seeds or intervals; imagined speech is a 50-word task without chance baseline or test counts; end-to-end takes 0.95 s per sentence (cascaded 0.24 s) with a bidirectional encoder unsuitable for online decoding.

title: A First Exploration of Neuromorphic OT-CFM for Multi-Speaker VSR
venue: Computer Vision – ECCV 2026, Lecture Notes in Computer Science
authors: Lin Chen; Jingping Fang; Hairui Liu; Chenyang Xu; Junhao Chen; Xiaorui Li; Weidong Cai; Xiaoming Chen
summary: Event input and a two-step OT-CFM decoder are standard; the DVS-Lip evaluation is behind: WER on an isolated-word set with no split details or seeds, and baselines that do not match their sources.
sensor: Event streams: event-camera recordings (DVS-Lip) and events converted from RGB video (AVA)
task: Visual speech recognition; multi-speaker scenes cut into single-speaker clips
vocabulary: Not stated; DVS-Lip has 100 isolated words
speaker: Not stated (DVS-Lip has 40 speakers; official protocol cited without split details)
key_result: 22.3 WER on DVS-Lip with 2-step OT-CFM vs 22.5 for 50-step diffusion at 25x lower latency; one run
limitations: DVS-Lip scored by WER with no split details or seeds; baseline rows do not match their sources; low-light gain uses RGB-converted events; two steps called optimal though ten score better.

title: AESSI: An Around-Ear Silent Speech Interface for Cross-Day Online Reuse without Test-Day Calibration
authors: Xiran Xu; Mochu Dong; Yujie Yan; Chenxi Wang; Yu Jiao; Jing Chen
summary: Around-ear cEEGrid system recognizing 25 fixed Mandarin sentences from silent articulation without test-day calibration; 92.24% mean accuracy on held-out later-day sessions and 98.00% in 250 live trials 21+ days later.
sensor: Bilateral around-ear cEEGrid electrodes (mixed EMG/EEG), 18 channels
speaker: Both
key_result: 92.24% accuracy, cross-day held-out sessions, no test-day calibration, chance 4%; 98.00% live (245/250)
limitations: Closed 25-sentence set only; mixed signal sources not separated; open-vocabulary conversation, walking, noise, long wear and patient use untested; live test used a single seed.

title: Affect Decoding in Phonated and Silent Speech Production from Surface EMG
authors: Simon Pistrosch; Kleanthis Avramidis; Zhao Ren; Tiantian Feng; Jihwan Lee; Monica Gonzalez-Machorro; Anton Batliner; Tanja Schultz; Shrikanth Narayanan; Björn W. Schuller
summary: Affect decoded from silent-articulation EMG, a design absent from 99 ledger studies (M08, ahead); it works within subject, nears chance across speakers, and is not separated from facial expression.
sensor: 8-channel bipolar facial/neck surface EMG (gel)
speaker: Both
key_result: Silent-only within-subject AUC 0.829; held-out-speaker EMG AUC 0.567-0.574
limitations: Small imbalanced cohort; facial expression and speech motor activity not separated; fixed task order; no independent-day, mobile or patient testing.

title: Articulatory movements influence electromagnetic wave transmission through the vocal tract
authors: Remi Blandin; Martin Laabs; Rudolf von Bunau; Bryn Lloyd; Silvia Farcito; Denys Nikolayev; Gabriela Hossu; Peter Birkholz; Dirk Plettemeier
summary: Physical modeling and measurement of contact RF transmission through the vocal tract for three sustained vowels in two participants; simulations qualitatively agree with measurements below about 3 GHz.
sensor: Two cheek-mounted bow-tie antennas with lab VNA; MRI models
task: Physical modeling of articulatory RF sensing
speaker: Not stated
key_result: Between-vowel transmission differences up to 15 dB near 1.5 GHz; repetition variation ~5-10 dB
limitations: Only two participants and three vowels; agreement mainly qualitative with no error metric; no recognition system, wearable device or patient use.

title: AVSRBench: A Multi-Condition AVSR Benchmark
authors: Rishabh Jain; Naomi Harte
summary: Zero-shot cross-corpus AVSR testing (M12) and a video-call test set (M11) are standard after WildVSR; each condition mixes several shifts, without repeated runs.
sensor: RGB camera and microphone (audio-visual)
vocabulary: Dataset-dependent; continuous open vocabulary (GRID fixed grammar)
speaker: Not stated
key_result: 0.79% AV WER on LRS3 (Llama-AVSR); visual-only WER 110.07% on RoomReader-AV (Auto-AVSR)
limitations: Uses fixed public checkpoints without retraining; camera-based AVSR rather than wearable SSI; no real-time or on-device measurement; limited speaker-split and statistical detail.

title: Brain-to-Speech: Prosody Feature Engineering and Transformer-Based Reconstruction
venue: Artificial Intelligence, Data and Robotics (E. Curry et al., eds.)
authors: Mohammed Salah Al-Radhi; Géza Németh; Andon Tchechmedjiev; Binbin Xu
summary: Same three parts and same Table 1 values as MiSTR (2025, same first two authors), not cited. Features (M06) and phase vocoder (M08) standard, unablated; no listener test (M12, behind).
sensor: Implanted sEEG depth electrodes
speaker: Not stated
key_result: PC 0.91, MCD 3.92, STOI 0.73, HNR 12.7 dB, tenfold cross-validation
limitations: Split unit and participant separation unspecified; neural prosody features not validated; no human intelligibility, WER or latency measurement.

title: Brain2Speech-Net: Fast and Intelligible Brain-to-Speech Synthesis Without Text Decoding
authors: Shreeram Suresh Chandra; Zexin Cai; Yu Tsao; Simon King; Berrak Sisman
summary: Text-free synthesis is shown, but its real time is throughput, not causal synthesis, unseen-sentence WER is 2.3 times the cascade, and intelligibility rests on ratings and ASR.
sensor: Intracortical microelectrode arrays (four recorded); 256 area-6v motor-cortex features (threshold crossings and spike-band power)
task: Speech synthesis from attempted speech without text decoding (offline)
vocabulary: Large-vocabulary prompted sentences; no lexicon or language model in the proposed model (cascade baselines use a 125k-word 5-gram LM)
speaker: One participant with ALS (Willett et al. 2023 dataset)
session: Recording sessions of the public dataset; session count not stated in the paper
key_result: Unseen-sentence Whisper WER 0.472 and PER 0.373 at RTF 0.532, against 0.206-0.229 WER at RTF above 1.8 for text cascades and 1.054 WER for a direct speech-unit baseline; MOS 3.34 on a 1-5 intelligibility rating; seen training sentences 0.068 WER.
limitations: Alignment uses future observations up to the end of the utterance, so synthesis is not causal; RTF without hardware or first-audio latency; intelligibility by rating and ASR, not listener transcription; one participant, one run, no seeds; targets, decoder and MCD reference all come from the same VITS model; released Phase 1 configuration selects on the official test split by default.

title: Comparison of sEMG Encoding Accuracy Across Speech Modes Using Articulatory and Phoneme Features
authors: Chenqian Le; Ruisi Li; Beatrice Fumagalli; Yasamin Esmaeili; Xupeng Chen; Amirhossein Khalilian-Gourtani; Tianyu He; Adeen Flinker; Yao Wang
summary: Applies an ECoG articulatory-versus-phoneme encoding comparison (Chartier 2018) to sEMG in three speech modes; the gain is small, mode contrasts are confounded, and no decoder is tested.
sensor: 8-channel lower-face/neck surface EMG
task: Forward encoding of sEMG from speech features
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: Gaddy replication voiced r 0.455 (SPARC) vs 0.443 (phoneme); main results plotted, not tabulated
limitations: Within-subject only; articulatory features inferred from paired voiced audio; DTW may inflate correlations; no actual decoding or synthesis gains tested.

title: Cross-Modal Masking for Robust Silent Speech Synthesis Using sEMG and Lipreading
authors: Eder del Blanco; David Gimeno-Gómez; Eva Navas; Carlos-D. Martínez-Hinarejos; Inma Hernáez
summary: Speech synthesis from fused sEMG and lip video is new to the ledger (M05, ahead); span masking (M03) adds a non-significant clean gain; seen speakers only (M12, behind).
sensor: 8 bipolar face/neck sEMG sensors plus RGB lip video
task: Speech synthesis from sEMG and video
speaker: Not stated
key_result: Not reported
limitations: No held-out-speaker test, listener test or repeated runs; masking not compared with whole-stream dropout of both streams; bitrate units unstated.

title: CS-ETS: Chaos-Inspired Samba-Based EMG-To-Speech Synthesis with Nonlinear Chaotic Losses
authors: Sajid Fardin Dipto; Tarikul Islam Tamiti; David Vergano; Luke Baja-Ricketts; Anomadarshi Barua
summary: Smaller chaos-inspired Samba-based EMG-to-speech model with nonlinear losses; WER improves modestly from 42.20% to 41.26% while parameters drop from 54.10M to 32.03M.
sensor: Existing 8-channel facial EMG corpus
vocabulary: Open-vocabulary EMG corpus; size not specified
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: 41.26% WER vs 42.20% baseline; 32.03M parameters
limitations: Single speaker and dataset; large acoustic-metric gains confounded by target-audio alignment applied only to the proposed output; insufficient split details and no confidence intervals.

title: Do EEG Foundation Models Transfer to Speech? A Benchmark on Overt and Imagined Speech Decoding
authors: Owais Mujtaba Khanday; Mohamed Baha Ben Ticha; Sanae Belfrouh; Marc Ouellet; Jose A. Gonzalez-Lopez
summary: Benchmark (M03) confirms earlier reports that LaBraM gains nothing on speech EEG; decoders (M06) sit far below same-corpus results; test-subject early stopping (M12).
sensor: Existing 64-channel scalp EEG
speaker: Both
key_result: BCIC2020-T3 within-subject balanced accuracy 25.7-30.2% (best EEGConformer 30.2%; LaBraM 27.7%; chance 20%); LOSO 18.9-20.2%, all at chance. UGR-MINDVOICE speech mode EEGNet 61.3% vs LaBraM 57.3%, EEGMamba 56.6% (chance 33.3%); 60-word identity at most 2.9% (chance 1.7%).
limitations: Findings for LaBraM repeat uncited earlier work; only two foundation models; within-subject scores far below same-corpus results; test subject used for early stopping on UGR-MINDVOICE; no seed repetition; 30 vs 60 word classes inconsistent; offline only.

title: EEG-Based Imagined Speech Decoding Using a Hybrid CNN-SNN Architecture
authors: Fatima Shalhoub; Mariam Al Mawla; Kabalan Chaccour; Iván López-Espejo; Hoda Fares
summary: CNN-to-LIF decoder (M06) is standard: a 2024 SNN-CNN inner-speech decoder precedes it; 80.13% on the validation subset is not comparable with the 82.6% competition test score (M12); no SNN ablation.
sensor: Existing 64-channel scalp EEG
vocabulary: 5 words/phrases (Hello, Help me, Stop, Thank you, Yes)
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: 80.13% five-class accuracy and 80.14% F1 on the public validation subset (750 trials, 15 subjects, subject-dependent), one run; competition winner 82.6% on the test trials
limitations: Validation subset used as test with no selection set; no dense-head ablation, chance level, per-subject scores or run variance; prior SNN-CNN inner-speech decoder uncited; no energy or online measurement.

title: EMG-to-Speech with Fewer Channels
authors: Injune Hwang; Jaejun Lee; Kyogu Lee
summary: Channel-reduction study for EMG-to-speech using exhaustive subset search and full-channel pretraining; best four-channel subsets reach about 47.2% WER versus roughly 35% with all eight channels.
sensor: Subsets of 8-channel face/neck surface EMG
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: 47.2% WER, best 4-channel subset (full-channel ~35%)
limitations: Single subject; subset selection not clearly independent of reporting; no repeated runs or physically built reduced-channel device.

title: iPhoneme: Brain-to-Text Communication for ALS Using ConformerXL Decoding
authors: Yoonmin Cha; Dawit Chun; Sung Park
summary: Behind: 26.61% WER is four times the 6.67% holdout baseline on the same recordings; the T15 best-result claim fails, the scoring split is unnamed and the gaze interface is untested.
sensor: Four implanted 64-electrode intracortical microelectrode arrays
vocabulary: 42 phoneme classes; word vocabulary not reported
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: 26.61% WER, 7.86% PER on an unnamed split (offline)
limitations: Scoring split unnamed while validation informs LM and decoder tuning; behind the 2.5% online WER on the same participant; single participant; noncausal model; latency protocol missing; gaze interface not user-validated.

title: Lip-Siri: Contactless Open-Sentence Silent Speech with Wi-Fi Backscatter
authors: Ye Tian; Haohua Du; Chao Gu; Junyang Zhang; Shanyue Wang; Hao Zhou; Jiahui Hou; Xiang-Yang Li
summary: Wi-Fi backscatter lip sensing (M05) and subword sentence output (M08) are standard; open-sentence decoding is untested, with no sentence-disjoint split and 36.87% WER.
sensor: Wi-Fi backscatter tag with software-defined radio transceivers
speaker: Both
key_result: 85.61% word accuracy, 36.87% sentence WER, random 80/20 split; new users 81.5-85.5%
limitations: Open-sentence decoding untested: random 80/20 split of 340 repeated sentences, no sentence- or word-disjoint test; WER above the visual baseline; power not measured; manual start/end clicks.

title: LipSody: Lip-to-Speech Synthesis with Enhanced Prosody Consistency
authors: Jaejun Lee; Yoori Oh; Kyogu Lee
summary: Pitch and energy predicted from lips, face and emotion (M06) is standard: Faces-to-Voices did it in 2025. Prosody metrics improve, WER does not; normalization change unablated.
sensor: Existing RGB facial video
speaker: Speaker-independent
key_result: 54.22% ABX preference; WER 22.5% vs 22.1% baseline, unseen-speaker LRS3
limitations: No WER improvement; oracle audio cues and normalization changes complicate comparisons; limited perceptual study reporting; no runtime evaluation.

title: Mechanistic Interpretability of Brain-to-Speech Models Across Speech Modes
authors: Maryam Maghsoudi; Ayushi Mishra
summary: Patching shows the decoder depends on donor activations, not that transfer runs through a compact subspace: kept regions score below the unpatched decoder, with no null and no held-out split.
sensor: Stereotactic intracranial EEG (VocalMind dataset), one participant
task: Interpretability of a speech-reconstruction decoder across vocalized, mimed and imagined speech (activation patching, interpolation, causal scrubbing)
vocabulary: Paired sentences across three speech modes; 200 sentences per condition in the winner analysis; acoustic output, no lexicon or language model
speaker: One participant (speaker-dependent)
key_result: Unpatched PCC 0.725 imagined, 0.752 vocalized, 0.569 mimed; full vocalized-to-imagined patch 0.954; kept convolutional subspace 0.666 against 0.564 for matched random blocks, below the unpatched imagined decoder
limitations: One participant and one architecture; no described train-test split, fold count or seeds; subspaces selected and scored on the same data; full patching replaces the recipient activation; no overt-trained transfer test and no null model; 96 to 120 convolutional winners reported for a 64-channel layer.

title: Multi-Subject Pretraining Enables Short-Calibration Personalization for Closed-Corpus Surface EMG Speech Decoding
authors: Chenqian Le; Beatrice Fumagalli; Yasamin Esmaeili; Xupeng Chen; Tianyu He; Nikasadat Emami; Adeen Flinker; Yao Wang
summary: Standard training recipe (M03) at larger scale: pretrain on 26, calibrate 3 min. The closed corpus carries the result: unseen sentences give 99.9% WER (M12, behind).
sensor: 8-channel lower-face/neck surface EMG
speaker: Both
key_result: 21.7% CER / 31.9% WER, pretrain + fine-tune, closed 50 sentences; 78.6% CER on unseen sentences
limitations: Evaluation sentences can appear in other subjects' pretraining; performance collapses on unseen sentences; offline only, healthy adults, no latency or electrode re-donning tests.

title: NasoVoce: A Nose-Mounted Low-Audibility Speech Interface for Always-Available Speech Interaction
venue: Proceedings of the 2026 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems (CHI '26)
authors: Jun Rekimoto; Yu Nishimura; Bojian Yang
summary: Nose-pad mic plus vibration sensor (M05) and dual-input fusion (M06) are standard; noise is added to the mic only, so the robustness claim is untested in real noise (M12, behind).
sensor: Nose-pad MEMS microphone and vibration sensor in smart glasses
speaker: Not stated
key_result: Not reported
limitations: ASR evaluation uses synthetic noise; in-the-wild testing only qualitative; fusion not fully streaming; whispered vibration signals remain weak.

title: Physiological Noise Augmentation Improves Non-Invasive Brain-to-Speech
authors: Benjamin Ballyk; Teyun Kwon; Miran Özdogan; Oiwi Parker Jones
summary: Artifact-remix augmentation repeats 2024 reference-signal mixing, gains 3.3 points (not 4.7) only with 10-trial averaging, barely beats white noise, and does not directly test the claimed invariance.
sensor: MEG with EOG and ECG reference sensors
speaker: Speaker-dependent
session: One subject; session assignment not stated
key_result: EEGNet accuracy 73.0% to 76.3% with PNA and 10-trial averaging, 10 classes
limitations: Single-subject imagined digits; EOG/ECG references required; gain only with 10-trial averaging; headline 4.7 points not in the tables (3.3); no invariance or significance test.

title: Relating the Neural Representations of Vocalized, Mimed, and Imagined Speech
authors: Maryam Maghsoudi; Rupesh Chillale; Shihab A. Shamma
summary: Cross-mode transfer and rank scoring are standard tests; one participant, unstated alignment to vocalized targets and mismatched nulls leave the hierarchy and linear-better claims unsupported.
sensor: Stereotactic intracranial EEG (public VocalMind dataset), 110 electrodes, one participant
task: Cross-mode spectrogram reconstruction from vocalized, mimed and imagined Mandarin speech with linear (ridge) and CNN-RNN decoders
vocabulary: 100 prompted sentences, two repetitions per mode; acoustic output, no lexicon or language model
speaker: One participant (speaker-dependent)
key_result: Rank AUC above chance: linear 0.32 and nonlinear 0.59 for vocalized-trained on vocalized; linear mimed-to-imagined -0.01; all envelope correlations above shuffled or shifted nulls
limitations: One participant; split, seeds, shuffle counts and alignment of silent trials to vocalized targets not reported; linear and nonlinear models differ in target representation and null

title: Silent Speech Interfaces in the Era of Large Language Models: A Comprehensive Taxonomy and Systematic Review
authors: Kele Xu; Yifan Wang; Ming Feng; Qisheng Xu; Wuyang Chen; Yutao Dou; Cheng Yang; Huaimin Wang
summary: Taxonomy and review of silent speech interfaces in the LLM era across neural, EMG, magnetic, ultrasound, optical, acoustic and RF sensing, with benchmark and dataset tables.
sensor: Review: multiple SSI sensing modalities
speaker: Not stated
key_result: Not reported
limitations: No reproducible review selection procedure; citation errors and mixed metric scales make its tables unsuitable for rankings or deployment claims.

title: SilentWear: an Ultra-Low Power Wearable System for EMG-based Silent Speech Recognition
authors: Giusy Spacone; Sebastian Frey; Giovanni Pollo; Alessio Burrello; Daniele Jahier Pagliari; Victor Kartsch; Andrea Cossettini; Luca Benini
summary: Neckband EMG with on-body inference at 20.5 mW (M13) but no on-device accuracy; repositioning recovery by labeled fine-tuning is standard (M03); sensor reused from 2025.
sensor: Dry textile neckband, 14-channel differential surface EMG
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: 59.3% silent balanced accuracy on held-out days (77.5% pooled-day), 9 classes; 2.47 ms inference
limitations: Only four subjects and subject-specific models; large drop on new days; no closed-loop user study, walking or false-trigger evaluation.

title: SLD-L2S: Hierarchical Subspace Latent Diffusion for High-Fidelity Lip to Speech Synthesis
authors: Yifan Liang; Andong Li; Kang Yang; Guochen Yu; Fangkun Liu; Lingling Dai; Xiaodong Li; Chengshi Zheng
summary: Codec-latent flow decoder (M06) is standard: quality lead rests on predictors that rate output above ground truth; WER trails V2SFlow; speaker similarity uses reference audio.
sensor: Existing RGB video (mouth crops)
speaker: Not stated
key_result: LRS3 WER 30.22%, UTMOS 4.21; listener naturalness 4.17 vs 3.88 (V2SFlow)
limitations: Needs reference audio for speaker identity; LRS3 WER trails V2SFlow, LipVoicer and Intelligible in its own table; small listener study; training compute reported but no inference runtime.

title: Soft Active EMG Interface for Machine Learning-Enabled Silent Speech Recognition
authors: Yuta Kurotaki; Shusuke Yamakoshi; Reitaro Yoshida; Yutaka Isoda; Tamami Takano; Yuji Isano; Yusuke Miyake; Kentaro Kuribayashi; Hiroki Ota
summary: Hand-pressed fingertip EMG (M05) is standard: privacy and noise benefits argued, not tested; 97.2% on 30 words rests on a random within-participant split with no session hold-out (M12, behind).
sensor: Hand-worn fingertip dry electrodes, 4-channel facial surface EMG
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: 97.2% mean within-participant accuracy on 30 silently articulated words, 3 participants, random class-stratified split; pooled three-participant model 92.1%
limitations: Random within-participant split with no session or participant hold-out; sample counts for two participants do not reconcile; privacy and noise claims untested; decoding on a PC with no latency, power or command success figure.

title: SoniSpeech: A Large-Scale Open-Vocabulary Tri-Modal Dataset for Wearable Silent Speech Interfaces
authors: Ruidong Zhang; Jiacheng Liu; François Guimbretière; Cheng Zhang
summary: Open-vocabulary acoustic sensing on glasses (M05) and a one-speaker paired corpus (M11) are standard; voiced-data gains follow 2020 EMG work; one-speaker, one-run tests lag the field (M12).
sensor: Eyeglass-frame ultrasound speakers/microphones (FMCW echoes), audio, video
speaker: Speaker-dependent
session: 360 sessions (180 per mode); 20 held-out test sessions per mode
key_result: 26.3% silent WER with mixed voiced/silent training (78.4% voiced-only training)
limitations: Single author in one quiet setting; population and everyday-environment generalization untested; baseline uses echoes only, not trimodal fusion; no latency or power measurements.

title: Toward Practical BCI: A Real-time Wireless Imagined Speech EEG Decoding System
authors: Ji-Ha Park; Heon-Gyu Kwak; Gi-Hwan Shin; Yoo-In Jeon; Sun-Min Park; Ji-Yeon Hwang; Seong-Whan Lee
summary: Not ahead on any component: consumer headsets and imagined-speech user identification predate it; no online accuracy, latency or split, so the real-time practical claim is unsupported.
sensor: Scalp EEG: BrainAmp 30 EEG + 2 EOG channels (wired); Emotiv EPOC X 12 channels (wireless)
task: Imagined-speech command classification with user identification and per-user fine-tuning
vocabulary: 4 commands (help me, tell me, bored, tired)
speaker: Speaker-dependent (per-user models), three participants
mode: Real-time application described; Table I not labelled online or offline
key_result: 62.00% wired and 46.67% wireless four-class accuracy (chance 25%), three participants, split not stated; no identification accuracy, latency or online accuracy
limitations: Three participants; no train/test split or definition of +/-; no identification, calibration, latency or online results; wired-wireless drop confounded by channel count, EOG input and recordings; consumer headsets and imagined-speech user identification predate it; rest-state gating undefined.

title: Toward Robust, Reproducible, and Widely Accessible Intracranial Language Brain-Computer Interfaces: A Comprehensive Review of Neural Mechanisms, Hardware, Algorithms, Evaluation, Clinical Pathways and Future Directions
authors: Dongyi He; Wai Ting Siok; Nizhuan Wang
summary: Review of intracranial language BCIs covering neural mechanisms, hardware, algorithms, evaluation and clinical pathways, proposing a composite weighted benchmark.
sensor: Review: intracortical arrays, ECoG, SEEG
speaker: Not stated
key_result: Not reported
limitations: Composite benchmark is unvalidated with author-chosen weights; narrative rather than systematic; some source attributions and mechanism claims need correction.

title: Transfer Learning from ImageNet for MEG-Based Decoding of Imagined Speech
venue: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging (ISBI)
authors: Soufiane Jhilal; Stéphanie Martin; Anne-Lise Giraud
summary: ImageNet transfer on MEG scalograms (M03) and the learned sensor projection (M06) are standard; the ablation is new; rest and reading-order confounds limit the binary tasks (M12).
sensor: 248-magnetometer MEG (non-invasive)
task: Closed-set imagined speech condition and vowel classification
speaker: Both
key_result: ResNet-18 full-window balanced accuracy: imagery vs silence 90.4% pooled / 77.5% LOSO; imagery vs silent reading 81.0% / 72.2%; three vowels 60.6% / 51.7% (chance 33%). Removing ImageNet weights costs 5.7-8.9 points.
limitations: ImageNet transfer on MEG scalograms was done before (Dash et al. 2020, cited only for imagined sentences); binary tasks contrast imagery with rest and with silent reading in fixed order; no EMG; no seeds; learned projection not compared with a sensor mosaic; offline only.

title: Zero-Shot Imagined Speech Decoding via Imagined-to-Listened MEG Mapping
authors: Maryam Maghsoudi; Shihab Shamma
summary: New pipeline (imagined MEG mapped to listened MEG, then a listened-trained word decoder), but no no-mapping or null-mapping word control, and a shared closed poem set confounds word decoding.
sensor: 157-channel whole-head MEG
speaker: Speaker-independent
key_result: Recall@1 up to ~9.1% (combined embeddings), 76 words, leave-one-subject-out
limitations: Small 76-word vocabulary from rhythmic stimuli by trained musicians; low SNR; non-portable MEG; not tested on natural continuous imagined speech.

title: A Convolutional Framework for Mapping Imagined Auditory MEG into Listened Brain Responses
venue: 2025 59th Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems, and Computers
authors: Maryam Maghsoudi; Mohsen Rezaeizadeh; Shihab Shamma
summary: Mapping imagined onto listened MEG (M06) is ahead in design, but the subject-calibrated CNN gain is unproven: no ablation, a channel-shuffling null, and r 0.0113 against 0.0063.
sensor: Whole-head KIT MEG, 157 axial gradiometers
task: Mapping imagined to listened auditory MEG
speaker: Both
key_result: 8-condition accuracy 50.7% (chance 12.5%); CNN mean r 0.0113 vs control 0.0063
limitations: Very small correlations, no speech or text reconstruction, 11 trained musicians in a shielded room, and incomplete implementation and split details.

title: A Parallel Ultra-Low Power Silent Speech Interface based on a Wearable, Fully-dry EMG Neckband
authors: Fiona Meier; Giusy Spacone; Sebastian Frey; Luca Benini; Andrea Cossettini
summary: A fully dry wearable EMG neckband with ultra-low-power BioGAP-Ultra classifies 8 silently articulated words for one healthy user at 68% accuracy, dropping to 54% on an unseen re-wearing session; acquisition plus BLE uses 22.2 mW.
sensor: Dry-electrode textile neckband, 14-channel EMG
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: Silent 68% (pooled 5-fold), 54% leave-one-session-out, chance 12.5%
limitations: Single participant, cue-aligned 1.4 s segments, no on-device inference reported, and no walking, natural conversation or patient testing.

title: A Silent Speech Decoding System from EEG and EMG with Heterogenous Electrode Configurations
authors: Masakazu Inoue; Motoshige Sato; Kenichi Tomeoka; Nathania Nah; Eri Hatakeyama; Kai Arulkumaran; Ilya Horiguchi; Shuntaro Sasai
summary: Pooled EEG/EMG pretraining lifts 64-word accuracy, but each test subject's training sessions, the patient's included, are in pretraining; the coordinate kernel is neither new nor best.
sensor: 63-channel scalp EEG plus 5 bipolar facial EMG channels (eego sports); pretraining also on g.Pangolin and g.SCARABEO EEG with 3 EMG channels
task: Closed-set silent word classification (64 Japanese words); English phoneme decoding as a transfer test
vocabulary: 64 Japanese words; English transfer set with a 9,828-word vocabulary
speaker: Eight healthy participants and one patient; per-participant session split; one novel healthy participant for calibration
session: Sessions 1-16 train, 17-18 validation, 19-20 test per participant; patient new-day data over three days
key_result: 64-word accuracy 95.3% healthy (vs 70.1% individual-data baseline) and 54.5% patient (vs 13.2%; chance 1.6%) with the subject-specific tokenizer pretrained on 220 h
limitations: Test subjects' training sessions, including the patient's, are in the pretraining data; one patient; no EEG-only or EMG-only model; no seed count; data volume confounded with devices and tasks; calibration values only in a figure; English transfer is EMG only.

title: An instantaneous voice-synthesis neuroprosthesis
authors: Maitreyee Wairagkar; Nicholas S. Card; Tyler Singer-Clark; Xianda Hou; Carrina Iacobacci; Lee M. Miller; Leigh R. Hochberg; David M. Brandman; Sergey D. Stavisky
summary: Closed-loop sentence voice from intracortical arrays holds for one participant; the design is standard, forced-choice and proxy-target metrics overstate intelligibility.
sensor: Four intracortical microelectrode arrays (256 electrodes) in ventral precentral gyrus
task: Real-time brain-to-voice synthesis with intonation and pitch control
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: Closed-set intelligibility 94.34%; question intonation 90.5%; emphasis 95.7%; ~60% open word intelligibility (press release)
limitations: Single participant; open intelligibility inconsistent; reviewed from preprint plus press release, not final Nature text.

title: An Introduction to Silent Paralinguistics
authors: Zhao Ren; Simon Pistrosch; Buket Coşkun; Kevin Scheck; Anton Batliner; Björn W. Schuller; Tanja Schultz
summary: Survey introducing silent paralinguistics: conveying emotion and speaking style, not only content, in silent speech, reviewing biosignal sensing modalities and open research problems without new experiments.
sensor: Survey of EEG, EMG, EMA, video, ultrasound, others
speaker: Not stated
key_result: Not reported
limitations: Narrative review with no reproducible literature search, quantitative synthesis or new evaluation; silent prosody lacks ground truth.

title: Articulatory Feature Prediction from Surface EMG during Speech Production
authors: Jihwan Lee; Kevin Huang; Kleanthis Avramidis; Simon Pistrosch; Monica Gonzalez-Machorro; Yoonjeong Lee; Björn Schuller; Louis Goldstein; Shrikanth Narayanan
summary: Articulatory route works on vocalized EMG but trails the mel baseline on WER; it exists for ECoG since 2019, and the electrode subset is never tested against equal-size alternatives.
sensor: 8-electrode surface EMG on face, jaw and neck (1000 Hz); paired 16 kHz laptop-microphone audio
task: Articulatory feature prediction (12-dim pseudo-EMA, pitch, loudness) from vocalized-speech EMG and speech synthesis from the predicted features
vocabulary: Open vocabulary, vocalized continuous English sentences (size not stated)
speaker: One male American English speaker; speaker-dependent
session: Gaddy corpus split: 200 validation and 99 test utterances
key_result: WER 15.5% and SpeechBERTScore 84.4 against 12.6% and 77.9 for the Gaddy mel-spectrogram baseline; four electrodes give 22.9% WER
limitations: Vocalized EMG of one speaker only; articulatory targets and references are inverted from the paired audio, not measured; baseline uses a different vocoder; electrode subset not compared with equal-size alternatives; no seeds, interval construction or latency.

title: Brain-to-Text Decoding: A Non-invasive Approach via Typing
authors: Jarod Lévy; Mingfang Zhang; Svetlana Pinet; Jérémy Rapin; Hubert Banville; Stéphane d’Ascoli; Jean-Rémi King
summary: Executed typing as the decoded action (M04) was ahead for MEG/EEG in 2025; keystroke-locked decoding (M06) and an n-gram LM (M07) are standard, and decoding needs known keystroke times.
sensor: Non-invasive MEG and EEG during typing
vocabulary: Spanish sentences of 5-8 words; 128 per session
speaker: Not stated
key_result: CER 32% MEG average (19% best), 67% EEG
limitations: Typing not speech; offline with keystroke alignment; healthy participants; MEG not wearable.

title: CAT-Net: A Cross-Attention Tone Network for Cross-Subject EEG-EMG Fusion Tone Decoding
venue: arXiv preprint (first page carries an AAAI 2026 copyright line)
authors: Yifan Zhuang; Calvin Huang; Zepeng Yu; Yongjie Zou; Jiawei Ju
summary: Cross-attention EEG-EMG fusion is new among EEG-EMG decoders but rests on a five-fold ablation with no seed count; no EEG-only result, and the subject adversary adds 0.41 points.
sensor: 64-channel NeuSen W EEG plus 5-site face/neck sEMG
speaker: Both
key_result: 85.10% leave-one-subject-out (silent, 4 classes); 88.08% 5-fold
limitations: No EEG-only or EMG-only model; cross-attention ablation is a five-fold average with no seed count, below a concatenation baseline; channel-selection data, early-stopping data, fold unit and seeds not stated.

title: Confidence-Based Self-Training for EMG-to-Speech: Leveraging Synthetic EMG for Robust Modeling
authors: Xiaodan Chen; Xiaoxue Gao; Mathias Quoy; Alexandre Pitti; Nancy F. Chen
summary: Synthetic EMG with confidence filtering (M03, standard) gives a small real-EMG gain, 23.30% to 21.87% WER on one speaker; large gains appear only on synthetic test EMG.
sensor: Existing 8-electrode surface EMG plus synthetic EMG
speaker: Not stated
key_result: WER 21.87% vs 23.30% baseline, real single-speaker vocalized EMG
limitations: Real EMG from only one speaker, no silent articulation evaluated, and figure/text inconsistencies and unclear splits remain.

title: Conformer-based Ultrasound-to-Speech Conversion
authors: Ibrahim Ibrahimov; Csaba Zainkó; Gábor Gosztolya
summary: Behind on M06: the Conformer reads beam lines of one frame, missing the multi-frame context mappers have used since 2020, with no objective gain; a small naturalness gain, no intelligibility test.
sensor: Ultrasound tongue imaging (TaL80, Micro system, 81.5 fps)
task: Ultrasound-to-speech synthesis: ultrasound frames to 80-band mel spectrogram, waveform by a pre-trained HiFi-GAN
vocabulary: Read TaL sentences; shared sentences 005-014 held out
speaker: Speaker-dependent, four TaL80 speakers (two female, two male)
session: Single session per speaker; train/development split 9:1 per speaker
key_result: Against a single-frame 2D-CNN, neither Conformer variant improves MSE or MCD (Conformer Base has higher MCD for all four speakers, significantly for three); MUSHRA naturalness 32 for Conformer with bi-LSTM against 28 for the baseline (p = 0.037), natural speech 96.
limitations: No multi-frame (3D-CNN) baseline; no intelligibility measure; no seeds or repeated runs; significance tests and corrections unstated; seen speakers and audible speech only; no inference latency despite the real-time claim.

title: Distinct Theta Synchrony across Speech Modes: Perceived, Spoken, Whispered, and Imagined
authors: Jung-Sun Lee; Ha-Na Jo; Eunyeong Ko
summary: Exploratory comparison of EEG theta-band functional connectivity across perceived, spoken, whispered and imagined speech in ten healthy subjects; no recognition performance is measured.
sensor: 128-channel active Ag/AgCl scalp EEG
task: Functional connectivity analysis across speech modes
speaker: Not stated
key_result: Not reported
limitations: No decoding evaluation, statistical tests are unspecified, PLI formula is inconsistent, and muscle or auditory confounds are not separated.

title: EEG-to-Voice Decoding of Spoken and Imagined speech Using Non-Invasive EEG
authors: Hanbeot Park; Yunjeong Cho; Hunhee Kim
summary: Drops DTW from an EEG-to-Mel generator (M06, standard) but tests only the ten trained classes (M12, behind); one frozen ASR both trains and scores it, and EEG output beats recorded-speech WER.
sensor: EGI 130-channel wet high-density scalp EEG
task: Speech synthesis and text from EEG
vocabulary: 10 closed classes per condition (words and sentences)
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: Imagined WER 47.48% at 2 s, 43.46% at 4 s, closed classes, before correction
limitations: Random splits include every class in training and test, imagined trials use overt audio as targets, and no unseen content, real-time use or clinical test is shown.

title: emg2speech: Synthesizing speech from electromyography using self-supervised speech models
authors: Harshavardhana T. Gowda; Daniel C. Comstock; Lee M. Miller
summary: Ports a 2023 ECoG recipe (text-to-speech HuBERT units, CTC) to EMG; phoneme guidance (M02) and covariance input (M06) are standard. Table 6 mixes listener and decoder scoring, so it ranks no route.
sensor: actiCHamp Plus wired gel surface EMG (31 channels)
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: Human-transcribed WER 50.82% (ALS, silent), 62.55% (healthy), unseen sentences
limitations: One subject per synthesis condition, high WER, wired gel electrodes, and no cross-day, re-wearing or everyday-use evaluation.

title: From Silent Signals to Natural Language: A Dual-Stage Transformer-LLM Approach
authors: Nithyashree Sivasubramaniam
summary: GPT-2 correction of one ASR transcript is neither first nor near the field: LLM correction of silent-EMG hypotheses already reached 12.2% WER on this benchmark; here 30% on ~100 utterances, one run.
sensor: 8-channel facial surface EMG from the existing Gaddy (Digital Voicing) corpus
task: Text from speech synthesized out of silent EMG, transcribed by a Transformer ASR and rewritten by GPT-2
vocabulary: Open-vocabulary read sentences of the Gaddy corpus; vocabulary size not stated
speaker: Not stated (corpus described as multi-speaker; test speakers not given)
session: Not stated; session embeddings used, session split not described
key_result: WER 36% (DeepSpeech) to 32.5% (Transformer ASR) to 30% (plus GPT-2) on about 100 test utterances, one run
limitations: Not the first LLM correction for silent EMG (12.2% WER earlier on the same benchmark); recognizer gain is a scorer swap; one transcript to GPT-2; test split not identified; no seeds, intervals or threshold selection data; 1000 Hz vs 16 kHz inconsistency.

title: IR-UWB Radar-Based Contactless Silent Speech Recognition with Attention-Enhanced Temporal Convolutional Networks
authors: Sunghwa Lee; Jaewon Yu
summary: Contactless IR-UWB radar in front of the lips with an attention-enhanced TCN classifies 50 English words for one user at 91.1% mean accuracy, versus 74.0% for a hand-crafted baseline.
sensor: Novelda IR-UWB radar near lips (5-10 cm)
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: 91.1% mean accuracy, 50 words, leave-one-session-out (baseline 74.0%)
limitations: Single participant, requires alignment before each utterance, no ablations or statistics, and no unseen users, words or free posture tested.

title: Landmark Guided Visual Feature Extractor for Visual Speech Recognition with Limited Resource
venue: Proceedings of the 4th International Workshop on Multimodal Human Understanding for the Web and Social Media (MUWS '25)
authors: Lei Yang; Junshan Jin; Mingyuan Zhang; Yi He; Bofan Chen; Shilin Wang
summary: Lip-landmark graph plus pixel fusion is a standard design (2020 precedent); the 0.90-point low-data gain comes from one unseeded run, and LRW 91.69% stays below 95.0%.
sensor: Existing broadcast RGB video (LRW); 20 lip landmarks derived from the same frames by a pretrained face-alignment network
task: Isolated-word visual speech recognition (lip reading) with a landmark-graph stream fused into a pixel front-end
speaker: LRW-ID: 20 held-out test speakers disjoint from training; following earlier LRW-ID settings they also form the validation set
key_result: LRW-ID one-third training: 86.65% vs 85.75% DC-TCN (one run); LRW 91.69%, below 93.2% / 95.0% (word boundary) of earlier LRW-only work
limitations: Graph-plus-pixel landmark fusion has a 2020 precedent; one run, no seeds; word-boundary input only in code; perturbation sizes unstated; no test without the landmark stream; 18.9% more parameters.

title: Large Language Models are Strong Audio-Visual Speech Recognition Learners
venue: IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech and Signal Processing (ICASSP)
authors: Umberto Cappellazzo; Minsu Kim; Honglie Chen; Pingchuan Ma; Stavros Petridis; Daniele Falavigna; Alessio Brutti; Maja Pantic
summary: Llama-AVSR is a strong engineering result but not a new design: VSP-LLM already had a frozen-encoder LoRA LLM decoder; SOTA margins are single-run and under 0.1 WER points.
sensor: Mouth ROI video plus audio
task: Sentence-level ASR, VSR and AVSR on LRS3 with a frozen LLM decoder
speaker: Not stated
key_result: LRS3 WER 0.77% AVSR and 0.79% ASR at 1,756 h; 25.3% VSR at 433 h (Table I)
limitations: One run per cell; comparison rows copied from other papers; labelled-hours accounting omits encoder pre-training; no inference cost

title: Lightweight Diffusion-based Framework for Online Imagined Speech Decoding in Aphasia
authors: Eunyeong Ko; Soowon Kim; Ha-Na Jo
summary: Diffusion EEG decoder (M06) standard: Diff-E lineage, no ablation, not smaller. Online use (M13) standard: one patient, 20 trials. M12: Table I overall row disagrees with class rows.
sensor: 64-electrode actiCAP slim scalp EEG
speaker: Speaker-dependent
session: One offline calibration session, then one online session
key_result: Author-reported 65% top-1 and 70% top-2 accuracy over 4 classes in 20 online trials (one participant); the per-class rows of Table I are inconsistent with this overall row; their percentages force five trials per class and give 50% / 80%.
limitations: One participant and one 20-trial online session; per-class trial counts not reported and the overall accuracy does not follow from the per-class values; no baseline, ablation, chance reference or cross-day test.

title: LipDiffuser: Lip-to-Speech Generation with Conditional Diffusion Models
authors: Julius Richter; Danilo de Oliveira; Tal Peer; Timo Gerkmann
summary: Diffusion decoder with per-frame MP-FiLM (M06) and audio-only pretraining (M02) are standard; quality and speaker-similarity leads rest on enhanced targets and a clean-reference enrollment.
sensor: Existing video (88x88 grayscale mouth crop); no new sensor
vocabulary: Open vocabulary English continuous speech (size not stated)
speaker: Not stated
key_result: WER 38%, NISQA 4.57, speaker similarity 0.63 on LRS3-CHiME3 at -10 dB (1321 test files)
limitations: Requires clean enrollment audio, which Table 1 takes from the clean reference; quality gains follow training on enhanced targets; no ablation of MP-FiLM or audio-only pretraining; cross-dataset claim without results.

title: LTA-L2S: Lexical Tone-Aware Lip-to-Speech Synthesis for Mandarin with Cross-Lingual Transfer Learning
authors: Kang Yang; Yifan Liang; Fangkun Liu; Zhenping Xie; Chengshi Zheng
summary: Mandarin lip-to-speech whose gain over Intelligible matches its English-initialization ablation; the tone components move CER little with no repeats reported, and pitch removal leaves TER at 40.9%.
sensor: Existing video (CN-CVS), 96x96 mouth crops
vocabulary: Mandarin continuous speech; size not stated
speaker: Speaker-independent
key_result: CER 61.2%, TER 40.9% on CN-CVS unseen-speaker split
limitations: Gain tied to English initialization; no repeats reported for the tone components; FunASR re-transcribed test labels without a real-audio floor; speaker-embedding source unstated; offline, voiced speech only.

title: MultiDiffNet: A Multi-Objective Diffusion Framework for Generalizable Brain Decoding
venue: arXiv preprint; preliminary version at the NeurIPS 2025 Workshop: Foundation Models
authors: Mengchun Zhang; Kateryna Shapovalenko; Yucheng Shao; Eddie Guo; Parusha Pradhan
summary: Diff-E-style decoder (M06) whose own ablation does not show diffusion helping; 1.01-point imagined-speech gain over EEGNet on two held-out subjects, normalized on scored trials (M03).
sensor: Existing 62-channel scalp EEG datasets
speaker: Both
key_result: Unseen-subject accuracy 11.62% vs EEGNet 10.61% (12.12% with Mixup), 11-class imagined speech
limitations: Near-chance accuracy, two held-out imagined-speech subjects, own ablation does not show diffusion helping, and unseen-subject normalization uses scored trials.

title: NaturalL2S: End-to-End High-quality Multispeaker Lip-to-Speech Synthesis with Differential Digital Signal Processing
authors: Yifan Liang; Fangkun Liu; Andong Li; Xiaodong Li; Chengshi Zheng
summary: DDSP prior and jointly trained vocoder (M06) are standard: joint waveform training predates it; quality leads its baselines, but LRS3 WER 30.4% trails the uncompared LipVoicer (21.4%).
sensor: Existing video (88x88 grayscale mouth crop); no new sensor
vocabulary: Open vocabulary English continuous speech (size not stated)
speaker: Not stated
key_result: WER 30.4% on LRS3 and 36.5% on LRS2, against 27.7%/33.5% for Lip2Speech Unit in the paper's tables and 21.4%/17.8% for LipVoicer in its own paper; highest predicted and rated quality among the compared systems.
limitations: Joint waveform training and reference-free use predate it; the joint-training ablation also removes DDSP and changes the vocoder corpus; run count and seeds not stated; LipVoicer omitted; baselines scored on supplied samples; speaker overlap not stated.

title: NeuroTTT: Bridging Pretrain–Downstream Task Misalignment in EEG Foundation Models via Test-Time Training
authors: Suli Wang; Yangshen Deng; Zhenghua Bao; Xinyu Zhan; Yiqun Duan
summary: SSL fine-tuning losses (M02) and test-time updates (M03) are standard: SSL-TTT never beats Tent; 0.59 balanced accuracy trails the 82.6% competition winner if scored on its test set.
sensor: 64-channel scalp EEG (existing dataset)
vocabulary: 5 phrases (hello, help me, stop, thank you, yes)
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: Balanced accuracy 0.5898 (CBraMod, Stage I + Tent), within-subject, 5 classes, BCIC2020-III; the 2020 competition winner reached 82.6% on the same corpus
limitations: Stage I and test-time effects not separated in tables; self-supervised test-time training never beats Tent; no seeds, significance tests, external baselines or test-time cost.

title: Non-invasive electromyographic speech neuroprosthesis: a geometric perspective
authors: Harshavardhana T. Gowda; Lee M. Miller
summary: Silent-EMG-to-text without vocalized pairing and SPD inputs are both standard: subvocal-only label training predates it, and 73.53% WER from one person is tested only against a near-chance baseline.
sensor: 31 monopolar surface EMG sites on face, jaw, chin, lips and neck; active gel electrodes, actiCHamp Plus amplifier, 5,000 Hz
task: Silent-articulation sentence decoding to phonemes and English words without vocalized recordings; appendix closed-vocabulary date sentences, NATO-code spelling, and wrist-EMG typing (EMG2QWERTY)
vocabulary: Over 6,500 unique words in about 11,000 sentences; 4-gram LM and lexicon from LibriSpeech-100 transcripts; appendix 67-word and 26-code tasks
speaker: One healthy participant for the main corpus; four for NATO codes; eight EMG2QWERTY users with personalized models
session: Sentence-disjoint split 8,000 / 1,000 / 1,970 by corpus order; session separation not stated
key_result: PER 48.47% and WER 73.53% on 1,970 held-out sentences, against 89.25% / 100% for a spectrogram input to the same GRU (chance PER 97.5%)
limitations: One participant; no seeds or repeated runs reported; near-chance baseline; no run on the public silent-EMG benchmark; subvocal-only label training predates it; no latency, cross-session or clinical test.

title: Poster: Recognizing Hidden-in-the-Ear Private Key for Reliable Silent Speech Interface Using Multi-Task Learning
venue: Companion of the 2025 ACM International Joint Conference on Pervasive and Ubiquitous Computing (UbiComp Companion '25)
authors: Xuefu Dong; Liqiang Xu; Lixing He; Zengyi Han; Ken Christofferson; Yifei Chen; Akihito Taya; Yuuki Nishiyama; Kaoru Sezaki
summary: Sensing, shared model and joint word-plus-identity output are each standard; whisper adds nothing over the 91.4% ultrasonic-only baseline, and impostors are training participants (M12 behind).
sensor: Modified ANC earbud in-ear microphone (whisper + ultrasound)
task: Spelling-based text entry and user authentication
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: 67.3% Top-1 word accuracy across 11 users; authentication TPR 81.76%, FPR 3.2%
limitations: Depends on whisper, three users fail badly, hardware is modified, and no replay/injection attacks or unseen-impostor tests are evaluated.

title: Pretraining Large Brain Language Model for Active BCI: Silent Speech
venue: Proceedings of the 33rd ACM International Conference on Multimedia (MM '25)
authors: Jinzhao Zhou; Zehong Cao; Yiqun Duan; Connor Barkley; Daniel Leong; Xiaowei Jiang; Quoc-Toan Nguyen; Ziyi Zhao; Thomas Do; Yu-Cheng Chang; Sheng-Fu Liang; Chin-Teng Lin
summary: In-domain EEG pretraining adds 4.3 points on 24 mouthed words (35.3% to 39.6%), one session, no seeds; Du-IN showed this earlier. Muscle artefact and new users remain untested.
sensor: 128-channel Neuroscan scalp EEG cap, 122 EEG channels, 1000 Hz (downsampled to 250 Hz)
task: Closed-set classification of silently articulated (mouthed) words from scalp EEG
vocabulary: 24 fixed English words; also 6 semantic groups
speaker: Speaker-dependent (per-participant fine-tuning; no unseen participant)
session: Cross-session: one held-out validation and one held-out test session per participant
key_result: 24-word accuracy 39.6% with pretraining vs 35.3% for the same model from scratch and 32.3% for TCNet (Table 1); 6-group accuracy 47.0% vs 42.2% (Table 2); one test session per participant, no seed count reported.
limitations: Pretraining and testing use the same 12 participants; no unseen-user or second-dataset test; no seeds, chance level or statistical test; mouthed articulation; the six muscle-noise reference electrodes are not used as an EMG control; semantic mean misprinted as 42.8% in Sec. 5.1 (Table 2 per-participant values average to 47.0%); dataset not yet released.

title: Reconstructing Unseen Sentences from Speech-related Biosignals for Open-vocabulary Neural Communication
authors: Deok-Seon Kim; Seo-Hyun Lee; Kang Yin; Seong-Whan Lee
summary: EEG+EMG fusion (M05) and overt-audio DTW targets (M02) are standard; the unseen-sentence claim lacks a cohort WER (M12), and no EMG-only arm or EMG regression is reported.
sensor: 128-channel actiCAP EEG plus 10 face/neck EMG channels
vocabulary: 474 cued English sentences; 39 phonemes plus silence
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: Overt phoneme accuracy 48.58% EEG+EMG, 36.83% EEG, held-out sentences, baseline 11%
limitations: Strongest evidence is overt/whispered, imagined results are from a representative subject, CER only for examples, and silent targets use overt audio.

title: RESOUND: Speech Reconstruction from Silent Videos via Acoustic-Semantic Decomposed Modeling
authors: Long-Khanh Pham; Thanh V. T. Tran; Minh-Tan Pham; Van Nguyen
summary: Decoder split (M06) and lip-reader text plus audio prompt (M07) are standard; WER gain comes from the lip reader, LRS3 WER level with LipVoicer, prosody leads confounded by the prompt.
sensor: Existing video (LRS2/LRS3) plus reference audio
vocabulary: English continuous speech; LRS3 over 50,000 words
speaker: Not stated
key_result: LRS3 WER 20.06 against 21.04 for LipVoicer in the paper's table and 21.4% in LipVoicer's own paper; LRS2 WER 28.55 against 17.04; without lip-reader text LRS3 WER is 27.49.
limitations: Source-filter synthesis, pitch and energy predictors and lip-reader text predate it; the prompt is a ground-truth audio segment with test-time source not stated; ablations remove modules in pairs; no seeds or repeated runs; baseline provenance and RTF hardware not stated.

title: Silent Speech Sentence Recognition with Six-Axis Accelerometers using Conformer and CTC Algorithm
authors: Yudong Xie; Zhifeng Han; Qinfan Xiao; Liwei Liang; Lu-Qi Tao; Tian-Ling Ren
summary: CTC decoder (M06), concatenated training sentences (M03) and six IMUs (M05) are standard: CTC silent-phrase decoding predates it; 97.17% is a word ratio on 4 people, split unstated.
sensor: Six 6-axis MEMS IMUs on face and neck
vocabulary: 16 English words, 2 English sentences, 8 Mandarin phrases
speaker: Both
key_result: 97.24% (words) and 97.16% (sentences) as correctly recognized words over total words, 4 participants, unstated split; the conclusion gives 97.17% for both. Single gyroscope axes 92.39-93.39% against accelerometer axes 87.62-92.42%.
limitations: Four participants and a closed vocabulary; split unit and speaker overlap not stated; blind scores only in a figure; few-shot sample count, CTC search and runs not stated; long test sequences likely concatenated; CTC silent-phrase decoding predates it.

title: Speaking Without Sound: Multi-speaker Silent Speech Voicing with Facial Inputs Only
venue: IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech and Signal Processing (ICASSP)
authors: Jaejun Lee; Yoori Oh; Kyogu Lee
summary: Face voices (M08) extend 2020 TTS and 2023 lip-to-speech designs to EMG; the pitch-flattening gain (M02) is within seed noise; silent WER 38.91% has no external baseline.
sensor: Existing facial/neck surface EMG plus target face image
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: Silent WER 38.91% with pitch flattening vs 40.12% without
limitations: Only one EMG participant; multi-user decoding and faithful personal-voice recovery not shown; main baseline is the same framework without flattening.

title: Subject-Independent Imagined Speech Detection via Cross-Subject Generalization and Calibration
authors: Byung-Kwan Ko; Soowon Kim; Seo-Hyun Lee
summary: Cyclic training and 10% target calibration (M03) are standard; uncalibrated detection is near chance (MCC 0.044–0.123), and labels are timed from overt speech.
sensor: Scalp EEG (device and channel count not stated)
task: Imagined-speech versus idle state detection (binary, 500-ms windows)
vocabulary: 2 classes (speech state vs idle); no words
speaker: Both (strict and calibrated leave-one-subject-out, subject-dependent)
key_result: Strict LOSO accuracy 0.670 (MCC 0.123, AUC 0.619) and 0.781 (MCC 0.382, AUC 0.801) after 10% target calibration, against 0.817 subject-dependent; six subjects
limitations: Labels timed from overt speech; cyclic gain rests on one configuration pair without seeds or pooled baseline; overlapping windows without a stated trial-level split; no chance level, calibration time or online test.

title: Towards Unified Neural Decoding with Brain Functional Network Modeling
authors: Di Wu; Linghao Bu; Yifei Jia; Lu Cao; Siyuan Li; Siyu Chen; Yueqian Zhou; Sheng Fan; Wenjie Ren; Dengchang Wu; Kang Wang; Yue Zhang; Yuehui Ma; Jie Yang; Mohamad Sawan
summary: Pooled sEEG training (M03) and region-token input with imputation (M06) are standard: both predate it (Du-IN, Chen 2024); no absolute accuracy is given and the baselines are weak checkpoints.
sensor: Implanted stereo-EEG depth electrodes
speaker: Both
key_result: Shared training gains of 5.10% / 4.97% (silent offline, participants 10/11)
limitations: Only five silent and two online participants, random sample splits, reduced unseen-subject accuracy, and bedside setup with implanted electrodes.

title: Transfer Learning for Covert Speech Classification Using EEG Hilbert Envelope and Temporal Fine Structure
authors: Saravanakumar Duraisamy; Mateusz Dubiel; Maurice Rekrut; Luis A. Leiva
summary: Overt-to-covert EEG transfer (M04) is not new, even on this dataset; the overt-only control is missing, the from-scratch baseline is unmatched, and 79.82% is tied to no fine-tuning fraction.
sensor: 64-channel scalp EEG (Brain Products LiveAmp 64), 500 Hz
task: Covert speech command classification with overt-speech pretraining
speaker: Speaker-dependent
session: Within-session random split (session boundary not stated)
key_result: 79.82% five-class covert accuracy after overt pretraining and output-layer fine-tuning on 15-30% covert data (fraction behind the mean not stated), against 66.94% from scratch; overt 86.44%; 15 participants, subject-specific
limitations: Transfer not new (Lee et al. 2022; the dataset study reported 61.78% overt-only on the same recordings); no overt-only condition or random-network control; from-scratch data amount and covert session split not stated; text's 20-point gain against 12.88 in the tables; printed means differ from row means; no feature ablation; same features reach 18.41% on a held-out subject in later work on the same data.

title: VSpeechLM: A Visual Speech Language Model for Visual Text-to-Speech Task
authors: Yuyue Wang; Xin Cheng; Yihan Wu; Xihua Wang; Jinchuan Tian; Ruihua Song
summary: Lip-timed phonemes into a codec LM (M06) are standard; Chem WER edges EmoDubber 12.5% vs 12.8%, no SyncNet scores, and the stated sync gains do not follow from Table 1.
sensor: Existing video; AV-HuBERT lip features (25 fps)
speaker: Chem single speaker; GRID 33 speakers (held-out speakers not stated)
key_result: WER 12.5% (Chem) and 18.3% (GRID) on speech synthesized from given text; EmoDubber 12.8% and 19.8% in the same table
limitations: Needs the script and a reference voice; no SyncNet lip-sync scores; table and text inconsistencies

title: Wireless Silent Speech Interface Using Multi-Channel Textile EMG Sensors Integrated into Headphones
authors: Chenyu Tang; Josée Mallah; Dominika Kazieczko; Wentian Yi; Tharun Reddy Kandukuri; Edoardo Occhipinti; Bhaskar Mishra; Sunita Mehta; Luigi G. Occhipinti
summary: Headphone-integrated textile EMG (M05) is standard, after a dry-electrode necklace; 96% on ten words is one random sample split over four people, speaker separation not stated.
sensor: 4-channel dry textile EMG electrodes in headphone earcups
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: 96% accuracy, 10 words, 4 participants, random sample-level 80/20 split (76.5% without filtering)
limitations: Only 4 participants with a sample-level random split; unseen users, other days, re-wearing, walking, latency and power consumption are untested.

title: A neural speech decoding framework leveraging deep learning and speech synthesis
authors: Xupeng Chen; Ran Wang; Amirhossein Khalilian-Gourtani; Leyao Yu; Patricia Dugan; Daniel Friedman; Werner Doyle; Orrin Devinsky; Yao Wang; Adeen Flinker
summary: Differentiable-synthesizer decoding (M06) and autoencoder guidance (M02) are standard: the group posted both in 2021. New here: 48-participant scale; naturalness and generalization untested.
sensor: Clinical subdural ECoG (43 low-density 8x8 grids, 5 hybrid-density), high-gamma 70-150 Hz
task: Overt word production in five elicitation tasks; ECoG-to-speech synthesis
speaker: 48 participants, per-participant models
key_result: Mean spectrogram PCC 0.806 non-causal and 0.797 causal (3D ResNet) over 48 participants
limitations: Test words recur in training; no listener test; no held-out-participant test; no chance level; split stated inconsistently

title: Advancing NAM-to-Speech Conversion with Novel Methods and the MultiNAM Dataset
authors: Neil Shah; Shirish Karande; Vineet Gandhi
summary: Compares ways to create target speech for converting non-audible murmur (NAM) to speech and releases the 7.96-hour MultiNAM dataset. Diff-NAM gives final WER 32.39%/38.94% for two speakers, below Lipvoicer but behind MFA-TTS (26.38%/32.61%).
sensor: Bluetooth digital stethoscope behind the ear (NAM vibration)
vocabulary: Read sentences from LJSpeech (size not stated)
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: Final WER 32.39%/38.94% (two speakers) for Diff-NAM vs 26.38%/32.61% for MFA-TTS
limitations: Only two healthy speakers whispering prompted text; data splits and test isolation unclear; no listening test, no patients, re-wearing, noise or latency evaluation.

title: AKVSR: Audio Knowledge Empowered Visual Speech Recognition by Compressing Audio Knowledge of a Pretrained Model
authors: Jeong Hun Yeo; Minsu Kim; Jeongsoo Choi; Dae Hoe Kim; Yong Man Ro
summary: The quantized audio memory (M02) is a standard memory-recall design; its gains repeat over a no-memory baseline, but the LRS3 state-of-the-art claim and the edge over distillation do not hold.
sensor: Camera (lip video)
speaker: Not stated
key_result: LRS3 WER 41.6% vs 46.1% no-memory baseline (BASE, 30 h) and 43.6% for distillation; LARGE 23.6% with 1,326 h pseudo-labels, behind SynthVSR Large at 18.2% without a language model on 3,068 h plus 3,652 h synthetic
limitations: Memory trained on 656 h of paired audio-text, so low-resource rows are not label-matched, and its data effect mixes size with in-domain LRS3 audio; single runs without seeds; language-model use of the proposed rows not stated; table-text inconsistencies (Tables VI, VIII, IX); offline benchmark only, no latency.

title: An Accurate and Rapidly Calibrating Speech Neuroprosthesis
authors: Nicholas S. Card; Maitreyee Wairagkar; Carrina Iacobacci; Xianda Hou; Tyler Singer-Clark; Francis R. Willett; Erin M. Kunz; Chaofei Fan; Maryam Vahdati Nia; Darrel R. Deo; Aparna Srinivasan; Eun Young Choi; Matthew F. Glasser; Leigh R. Hochberg; Jaimie M. Henderson; Kiarash Shahlaie; Sergey D. Stavisky; David M. Brandman
summary: Reaches 2.5% online large-vocabulary WER and 248 h of home use in one participant; rapid calibration is a cross-study claim and the 97.5% conversation accuracy matches the Copy Task figure.
sensor: Four 64-electrode intracortical microelectrode arrays in precentral gyrus
task: Attempted speech to text with personalized TTS output
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: Copy-task WER 2.5% at 31.6 wpm (125k words); conversation WER 3.7%
limitations: Single participant; rate well below natural speech; researcher needed to set up; long-term ALS progression effects unknown.

title: Let There Be Sound: Reconstructing High Quality Speech from Silent Videos
venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence (AAAI-24)
authors: Ji-Hoon Kim; Jaehun Kim; Joon Son Chung
summary: HuBERT-unit, pitch and energy targets (M02) and flow post-net (M06) are standard, after ReVISE and VCVTS; GRID WER 17.07% vs 17.62%; seen-speaker tests only (M12 behind).
sensor: Camera (lip video)
speaker: Seen speakers only (GRID 33, Lip2Wav 2)
key_result: GRID WER 17.07% vs 17.62% for VCA-GAN (scorer 12.20% on real speech) but MOS 4.46 vs 3.46 naturalness and 4.63 vs 4.10 intelligibility; two-speaker Lip2Wav WER 34.71% vs 48.73%; later LRS3 re-runs (a dataset the paper did not use, different scorers): 79.7% and 84.08% WER on unseen speakers
limitations: Test sets drawn from the training speakers (GRID 80/10/10 over all 33 speakers, Lip2Wav 2 speakers split 80/10/10); single runs; baselines retrained by the authors (SVTS reproduced); unit targets follow ReVISE (2022) and unit-plus-pitch decomposition follows VCVTS (2022), neither cited; speaker identity from a table of training speakers.

title: LipVoicer: Generating Speech from Silent Videos Guided by Lip Reading
venue: The Twelfth International Conference on Learning Representations (ICLR 2024)
authors: Yochai Yemini; Aviv Shamsian; Lior Bracha; Sharon Gannot; Ethan Fetaya
summary: Lip-reader text conditioning (M07) is new but standard: words come from the lip reader (19.1% reading WER becomes 21.4%; 86.2% unguided), and no cascade control is run.
sensor: Camera (lip video)
speaker: Not stated
key_result: LRS3 WER 21.4% (lip reader 19.1%; ground-truth text 5.4%; no ASR guidance 86.2%); LRS2 17.8%.
limitations: Words come from the lip reader; output WER is very sensitive to the guiding ASR (Table 11); no cascade control; evaluation ASR from the same work as the lip reader; no seeds; speaker overlap not stated; offline diffusion with hundreds of steps.

title: Online speech synthesis using a chronically implanted brain–computer interface in an individual with ALS
authors: Miguel Angrick; Shiyu Luo; Qinwan Rabbani; Daniel N. Candrea; Samyak Shah; Griffin W. Milsap; William S. Anderson; Chad R. Gordon; Kathryn R. Rosenblatt; Lora Clawson; Donna C. Tippett; Nicholas Maragakis; Francesco V. Tenore; Matthew S. Fifer; Hynek Hermansky; Nick F. Ramsey; Nathan E. Crone
summary: Closed-loop word synthesis (M06) from a chronic ECoG implant in ALS (M13) holds on six keywords at 80% listener accuracy; standard designs, one participant, stability untested.
sensor: 2 ECoG grids, 64 selected channels
task: Online word synthesis from overt speech, six-keyword closed vocabulary
speaker: One participant with ALS (dysarthria)
session: Trained on 10 days over 6 weeks; tested in 3 online sessions 5.5 months later
mode: Overt speech; closed loop with delayed playback
key_result: 80% six-choice listener identification (chance 16.7%); natural speech 99.8%
limitations: One participant; closed vocabulary; no per-session results; exclusions uncounted; requires vocalization

title: Ultrasensitive Textile Strain Sensors Redefine Wearable Silent Speech Interfaces with High Machine Learning Efficiency
authors: Chenyu Tang; Muzi Xu; Wentian Yi; Zibo Zhang; Edoardo Occhipinti; Chaoqun Dong; Dafydd Ravenscroft; Sung-Min Jung; Sanghyo Lee; Shuo Gao; Jong Min Kim; Luigi G. Occhipinti
summary: Standard sensor (M05) and decoder (M06): one throat strain channel, small CNN. 95.25% on 20 words, with split grouping and production mode unstated, does not show silent, session-independent decoding.
sensor: One graphene-on-textile strain sensor with ordered microcracks in a throat choker; potentiostat readout at 1 V, 500 Hz
task: Isolated word classification from 3-s single-channel strain windows with a 1D residual CNN
vocabulary: 20 frequent English words; 10 confusable words; 5 long words at three reading speeds
speaker: Three participants pooled; one further participant for few-shot transfer
session: Not stated; 100 samples per word split 80/20 without stated session grouping
mode: Offline; production mode (mouthed or voiced) not stated
key_result: 95.25% on 20 words, 93% on 10 confusable words, 96% on 5 long words; 80% with 15-20 and 90% with 30 fine-tuning samples per class on a new user or new words.
limitations: Split grouping, chance level and repeated runs not reported; production mode not stated; no sensor, channel or augmentation ablation; no on-device latency or power.

title: Unvoiced: Designing an LLM-assisted Unvoiced User Interface using Earables
venue: Proceedings of the 22nd ACM Conference on Embedded Networked Sensor Systems (SenSys '24), pp. 784-798
authors: Tanmay Srivastava; Prerna Khanna; Shijia Pan; Phuc Nguyen; Shubham Jain
summary: Twin-IMU earable captures jaw motion during unvoiced speech; spectrograms are transcribed by Whisper and gaps filled by GPT-4, giving 93-99% task completion and 0.07-0.14 WER across 19 users.
sensor: Twin-IMU earable (jaw motion accelerometer and gyroscope)
task: Unvoiced command and phrase recognition via spectrogram generation
vocabulary: Task phrases, 20 commands, digits, 30 general phrases, 50 unseen words
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: 93.1-98.6% task completion; WER 0.07 (seen phrases), 0.14 (unseen words); 19 participants
limitations: Per-user models trained with audible samples; LLM correction leans on language priors; latency and power unreported; prototype only.

title: Whisper-Flamingo: Integrating Visual Features into Whisper for Audio-Visual Speech Recognition and Translation
authors: Andrew Rouditchenko; Yuan Gong; Samuel Thomas; Leonid Karlinsky; Hilde Kuehne; Rogerio Feris; James Glass
summary: Whisper-Flamingo is a well-engineered combination of prior parts; its clean LRS3 gain disappears at beam 1, and one model trails per-pair models in noisy translation (20.5 vs 20.8 BLEU).
sensor: Mouth crops; log-Mel audio
task: Sentence-level AVSR on LRS3 and audio-visual En-X speech translation on MuAViC with Whisper and AV-HuBERT features
speaker: Not stated
key_result: LRS3 0 dB babble WER 5.6% vs 11.7% audio-only (beam 15, 433 h); MuAViC noisy average BLEU 20.5 vs 18.6 audio-only and 20.8 per-pair AV-HuBERT (Table 4)
limitations: Single runs; recreated noise files; clean gain depends on beam size (arXiv v3); fusion ablation on one model size

title: A high-performance neuroprosthesis for speech decoding and avatar control
authors: Sean L. Metzger; Kaylo T. Littlejohn; Alexander B. Silva; David A. Moses; Margaret P. Seaton; Ran Wang; Maximilian E. Dougherty; Jessie R. Liu; Peter Wu; Michael A. Berger; Inga Zhuravleva; Adelyn Tu-Chan; Karunesh Ganguly; Gopala K. Anumanchipalli; Edward F. Chang
summary: Text, voice and avatar from ECoG in one participant hold as a demonstration; sensor and decoder are standard, and an LM trained on the test pool inflates the text result.
sensor: 253-channel high-density ECoG array over sensorimotor and temporal cortex
task: Silent attempted speech to text, speech synthesis and avatar
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: Real-time median WER 25.5%, PER 18.5%, 78.3 wpm; 50-phrase set WER 4.92% (offline)
limitations: Single participant; AAC results offline; synthesized speech on general sentences has 54.4% perceptual WER; lab-based use.

title: A high-performance speech neuroprosthesis
authors: Francis R. Willett; Erin M. Kunz; Chaofei Fan; Donald T. Avansino; Guy H. Wilson; Eun Young Choi; Foram Kamdar; Matthew F. Glasser; Leigh R. Hochberg; Shaul Druckmann; Krishna V. Shenoy; Jaimie M. Henderson
summary: Large-vocabulary attempted-speech decoding in one participant holds; sensor, decoder and LM are now field standard, but the spiking attribution and cross-study ratios outrun the evidence.
sensor: Four intracortical microelectrode arrays (areas 6v and 44)
task: Attempted-speech (vocalized and mouthed) sentence decoding to text
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: Real-time WER 23.8% (vocalized) / 24.7% (silent) at 125k words; 9.1% / 11.2% at 50 words; 62 wpm
limitations: Single participant, daily recalibration, researcher-operated; 24% WER judged insufficient for everyday use by the authors.

title: Adaptation of Tongue Ultrasound-Based Silent Speech Interfaces Using Spatial Transformer Networks
authors: László Tóth; Amin Honarmandi Shandiz; Gábor Gosztolya; Tamás Gábor Csapó
summary: STN-only adaptation (M03) closes 75-76% of the retraining gap, not the 88% the abstract states; untested against lower-layer adaptation; dev-set MSE only (M12 behind).
sensor: Micro ultrasound tongue probe with fixing headset
speaker: Both
key_result: STN-only adaptation closes 75-76% of the gap between no adaptation and full retraining (2D CNN, MSE); adding the output layer closes 88% (three speakers) and 92% (four sessions of one speaker); development or unnamed split, single runs
limitations: No comparison with lower-layer adaptation at matched size; adaptation data per run not stated, only implied by the 85:10:5 split; mel-spectrogram MSE only, no held-out test, listening or intelligibility score; random split with unstated unit; no seeds or variance; voiced read speech only; session data much shorter than the base session.

title: Audio-visual video-to-speech synthesis with synthesized input audio
authors: Triantafyllos Kefalas; Yannis Panagakis; Maja Pantic
summary: A second synthesis pass on first-pass speech (M06) and modality dropout (M03) are standard; gains are small and inconsistent, earlier systems keep lower WER, and no equal-training control exists.
sensor: Camera (mouth video); synthesized audio from a first-stage model as a second input
vocabulary: GRID fixed 51-word vocabulary; TCD-TIMIT and LRW larger vocabularies
speaker: Both
key_result: Best WER 3.67% on GRID 4 seen speakers; 17.69% on GRID unseen speakers against 16.05% for an earlier end-to-end system; 14.24% on LRW against 12.90% for SVTS
limitations: No equal-training control for the second pass; training-set synthesized audio comes from a base model fitted to the same set; no listener test; single runs without seeds.

title: Auto-AVSR: Audio-Visual Speech Recognition with Automatic Labels
venue: IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech and Signal Processing (ICASSP)
authors: Pingchuan Ma; Alexandros Haliassos; Adriana Fernandez-Lopez; Honglie Chen; Stavros Petridis; Maja Pantic
summary: ASR transcripts as training labels (M02) are standard (Afouras 2020, Ma 2022); scale cuts LRS3 VSR WER to 19.1%, but no run spread is reported and USR 2.0 reaches 17.6%.
sensor: Video camera (lip region) and microphone
task: Visual, audio and audio-visual speech recognition
speaker: Speaker-independent
key_result: LRS3 WER: VSR 19.1%, ASR 1.0%, AV-ASR 0.9%; LRS2 VSR 14.6%
limitations: ASR-label design predates it (Afouras 2020, Ma 2022); no run count, seeds or spread reported; unnamed baseline for the 30% claim; babble noise in training and test; overt speech only.

title: Decoding speech perception from non-invasive brain recordings
authors: Alexandre Défossez; Charlotte Caucheteux; Jérémy Rapin; Ori Kabeli; Jean-Rémi King
summary: Contrastive M/EEG decoding (M06) and subject-layer pooling (M03) were ahead in 2022 and are now standard; tests reuse training participants, and EEG headline and EEG zero-shot claims outrun the data.
sensor: Non-invasive MEG (208/273 sensors) and EEG (60/128 channels)
vocabulary: Natural stories and sentences; 190-1,842 candidate segments
speaker: Not stated
key_result: MEG top-1 up to 41.3% average; top-10 up to 70.7%; EEG top-10 17.7-25.7%
limitations: Perception not production; retrieval from fixed candidates; MEG not wearable; EEG performance low.

title: EchoSpeech: Continuous Silent Speech Recognition on Minimally-obtrusive Eyewear Powered by Acoustic Sensing
authors: Ruidong Zhang; Ke Li; Yihong Hao; Yufan Wang; Zhengnan Lai; François Guimbretière; Cheng Zhang
summary: Glasses-mounted inaudible FMCW sonar recognizes silent speech from facial skin echoes: 4.5% WER on 31 commands and 6.1% on connected digits in 12 users, with walking/noise tests and a 73.3 mW demo.
sensor: Glasses-mounted speakers and microphones (inaudible FMCW active acoustic sensing)
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: WER 4.5% commands, 6.1% digits; 16.8% walking without mobile data
limitations: Closed vocabulary; needs user fine-tuning (~40% WER without); sensitive to glasses slippage; no activation detection.

title: High-Quality Automatic Voice Over with Accurate Alignment: Supervision through Self-Supervised Discrete Speech Units
authors: Junchen Lu; Berrak Sisman; Mingyang Zhang; Haizhou Li
summary: An automatic voice-over system that supervises alignment by predicting self-supervised discrete speech units from text and lip video, improving lip-sync and speech quality on a single-speaker dataset. Not an SSI paper.
sensor: Camera (lip video) plus text script
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: WER 24.7%, LSE-C 6.81, LSE-D 7.56, MOS 3.98 on single-speaker Chem dataset
limitations: Validated only on one single-speaker dataset; requires text scripts and pretrained unit tokenizer and vocoder; no multi-speaker or in-the-wild testing.

title: Improving the Gap in Visual Speech Recognition Between Normal and Silent Speech Based on Metric Learning
authors: Sara Kashiwagi; Keitaro Tanaka; Qi Feng; Shigeo Morishima
summary: Joint normal-silent training does most of the gap closing; the viseme KL terms add 0.93 WER points with no run count reported, so the metric-learning gain is not established.
sensor: Single frontal camera; Dlib lip crops
task: Closed-set phrase recognition from silent and normal lip video
speaker: Held-out speakers (20/8/11 split; disjointness not stated)
key_result: Silent WER 9.97% vs 12.91% two-mode baseline and 22.55% normal-only; run count not reported
limitations: No run count or spread for Table 1; selection split not stated; 10 fixed phrases; no comparison with other overt-silent training methods.

title: Intelligible Lip-to-Speech Synthesis with Speech Units
authors: Jeongsoo Choi; Minsu Kim; Yong Man Ro
summary: Unit target (M02) and unit-conditioned vocoder (M06) are standard; units cut LRS3 WER 21.8 points, AV-HuBERT 20.4 more, the vocoder 0.3; unit gain untested on AV-HuBERT, single runs.
sensor: Camera (lip video; optional AV-HuBERT encoder); speaker embedding from a speech segment
speaker: Speaker-independent on LRS3 (unseen-speaker split); LRS2 overlap unknown
key_result: LRS3 ASR WER 29.8% with the AV-HuBERT encoder (50.2% with ResNet-18); speech units cut WER from 72.5% to 50.7% (21.8 points) and AV-HuBERT a further 20.4 points; single runs
limitations: Single runs, no seeds; speaker embedding from an unspecified speech segment; unit gain untested with the AV-HuBERT encoder; the 20-clip MOS (4.40) is of the non-AV-HuBERT variant and V2SFlow's listeners (2.46, variant unstated) do not confirm it.

title: IR-UWB Radar-Based Contactless Silent Speech Recognition of Vowels, Consonants, Words, and Phrases
authors: Sunghwa Lee; Younghoon Shin; Myungjong Kim; Jiwon Seo
summary: FERASEC is a standard engineered radar front end with a large gain over 2016 features; phoneme novelty holds only for consonant syllables, and evaluation is within-speaker.
sensor: Two IR-UWB radars facing lips and below chin
speaker: Within-speaker; 20 participants for syllables, 4 for words and phrases
key_result: 86.47% vowels, 81.59% consonants, 88.95% words, 96.88% phrases (leave-one-out CV, upper radar)
