limitations: Controlled lab study with prompted closed-set items and limited speaker diversity; sensitive to user alignment and tooth blockage; no open vocabulary or conversational speech tested.

title: Jointly Learning Visual and Auditory Speech Representations from Raw Data
authors: Alexandros Haliassos; Pingchuan Ma; Rodrigo Mira; Stavros Petridis; Maja Pantic
summary: RAVEn's asymmetric momentum-teacher objective (M03) ties AV-HuBERT at Large with 30 h (32.5%); its lead comes with self-training (M02), whose pseudo-label decoding is not stated.
sensor: Grayscale mouth ROI, 25 fps; raw 16 kHz audio
task: Self-supervised audio-visual pre-training for lip reading (VSR) and ASR
speaker: Speaker-independent LRS3 test (test speakers disjoint from training)
key_result: LRS3 VSR WER 23.8% (Large, 30 h labelled, self-training and LM); 32.5% without, equal to AV-HuBERT
limitations: Single runs without seeds; ablations on Base and the validation set only; pre-training/test overlap not stated

title: Knowledge Distilled Ensemble Model for sEMG-based Silent Speech Interface
venue: arXiv preprint (submitted to the IEEE Region 8 Student Paper Contest 2023)
authors: Wenqiang Lai; Qihan Yang; Ye Mao; Endong Sun; Jiangnan Ye
summary: Ensemble-to-student distillation (M02, M06, M13) is standard: same-modality distillation predates it; 85.9% is one unseeded split of unstated unit, and 7x smaller is against six models.
sensor: 3-channel facial sEMG (BITalino, adhesive Ag/AgCl electrodes)
speaker: Five male speakers pooled; split unit not stated
key_result: 85.9% on 26 NATO words (one 4:1:1 split, unit not stated) vs 81.2% for one ResNet1D; 21.1 MB and 0.12 ms per sample on a GPU vs 147.9 MB and 2.50 ms for the six-model ensemble.
limitations: Same-modality distillation predates it; no student-without-teacher control; no seeds; split unit not stated; five male speakers; no on-device measurement.

title: Large-scale unsupervised audio pre-training for video-to-speech synthesis
authors: Triantafyllos Kefalas; Yannis Panagakis; Maja Pantic
summary: Audio-only decoder pre-training (M03) is standard after TTS decoder transfer; it lowers WER in 7 of 16 pairs, earlier systems keep lower WER, and no equal-training control or listener test exists.
sensor: Camera (mouth-region video)
speaker: Both
key_result: Paper's models: PESQ 1.30-2.07, STOI 0.478-0.720, WER 2.66%-41.00% across GRID, TCD-TIMIT and LRW; audio pre-training lowers WER in 7 of 16 model and split pairs; earlier systems keep lower WER on all four WER splits.
limitations: WER improvements not consistent; objective benchmark metrics only, with no human listening tests, latency or real-world robustness evaluation.

title: LipLearner: Customizable Silent Speech Interactions on Mobile Devices
venue: Proceedings of the 2023 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems (CHI '23)
authors: Zixiong Su; Shitao Fang; Jun Rekimoto
summary: All three changed components are standard: on-device few-shot head untested against prototypes or fine-tuning; voiced enrollment loses 5.6 points; visual KWS predates it uncited.
sensor: Smartphone front camera (lip video)
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: 98.8% five-shot (81.7% one-shot) accuracy, 30 commands, mobile app; ~422 ms on-device latency
limitations: Modest vocabulary and study scale; confuses similar commands, requires visible lips, and incremental learning adds user burden.

title: RobustL2S: Speaker-Specific Lip-to-Speech Synthesis exploiting Self-Supervised Representations
authors: Neha Sahipjohn; Neil Shah; Vishal Tambrahalli; Vineet Gandhi
summary: SSL-feature target (M02) and Seq2Seq-to-unit-vocoder decoder (M06) are standard after ReVISE; GRID-4S WER 11.21% is set against baselines scored with other ASRs.
sensor: Camera (lip video)
vocabulary: GRID 51 words; TCD-TIMIT 375 sentences per speaker; Lip2Wav over 5000 words
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: STOI 0.596, ESTOI 0.452, WER 29.03 on TCD-TIMIT-3S
limitations: Speaker-dependent or seen-speaker evaluation only; limited prosody modeling; no real-time or on-device deployment.

title: Semantic reconstruction of continuous language from non-invasive brain recordings
authors: Jerry Tang; Amanda LeBel; Shailee Jain; Alexander G. Huth
summary: LM candidates scored by encoding-model likelihood (M06) were ahead in 2022, as the authors claim; the scorer is now overtaken. GPT prior (M07) is standard; one pilot-touched test story limits M12.
sensor: 3T BOLD fMRI
task: Semantic language decoding (perceived speech, imagined speech, silent film)
speaker: Not stated
key_result: 72-82% of perceived-speech time-points decoded above chance (BERTScore); WER 0.92-0.94
limitations: One perceived test story, used in S3 pilots; three subjects with 16 h each; laboratory fMRI; meaning, not exact words.

title: Speech Reconstruction from Silent Tongue and Lip Articulation By Pseudo Target Generation and Domain Adversarial Training
authors: Rui-Chen Zheng; Yang Ai; Zhen-Hua Ling
summary: DTW pseudo targets (M02) follow prior EMG target transfer; the mode discriminator (M03) is untested by its ablation; silent MCD/STOI use self-made references and 18 speakers are dropped.
sensor: Ultrasound tongue imaging plus optical lip camera
speaker: 81 TaL speakers; utterance-level split, so test speakers also appear in training; 18 speakers dropped from the silent test
key_result: Silent mode on retained speakers: WER 43.114% vs 59.960% for TaLNet (iFLYTEK ASR), MOS 3.330 vs 2.990; vocalized WER 17.309% vs 26.890%
limitations: Silent MCD/STOI scored against the method's own vocoded pseudo targets; 18 of 81 speakers excluded by the method's DTW cost; the w/o DAT ablation also removes vocalized training; single runs, no seeds; prior DTW target transfer in EMG uncited.

title: WESPER: Zero-shot and Realtime Whisper to Normal Voice Conversion for Whisper-based Speech Interactions
venue: Proceedings of the 2023 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems (CHI '23)
authors: Jun Rekimoto
summary: WESPER trains a whisper-to-normal converter with no paired data (M02, ahead); its unit route (M06) is untested against baselines, and its ASR gain trails a recognizer fine-tuned on labelled whisper.
sensor: Ordinary microphone (whispered speech)
speaker: Speaker-independent
key_result: WER 44.70 to 26.68 (CER 28.38 to 12.70) on wTIMIT whispers, Google ASR
limitations: Relies on whispered rather than truly silent speech and is evaluated on whisper datasets, not silent-speech benchmarks or broad public use.

title: Zero-Shot Personalized Lip-to-Speech Synthesis with Face Image Based Voice Control
authors: Zheng-Yan Sheng; Yang Ai; Zhen-Hua Ling
summary: Face-image voice control (M07) and VAE/cross-modal training (M03) are standard: Facetron did face-derived zero-shot voice on GRID in 2021; face EER 36.72 vs 26.57 with reference audio; no WER.
sensor: Camera (lip video plus face image)
speaker: Speaker-independent
key_result: Unseen GRID speakers (13): face-image control EER 36.72 vs 26.57 with reference speech, MOS-FVM 3.133 vs 3.172; ESTOI 0.389; no ASR word error reported.
limitations: Face-derived zero-shot voice predates it (Facetron 2021); no WER; Table 2 scores the reference-speech variant; Griffin-Lim waveform; GRID only, no seeds; overlap of GRID with pretraining identities not stated.

title: Distinguishing Homophenes Using Multi-Head Visual-Audio Memory for Lip Reading
venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence
authors: Minsu Kim; Jeong Hun Yeo; Yong Man Ro
summary: Audio memory (M02) and multi-head, multi-depth addressing (M06) are standard: the memory is the same group's ICCV design, head and depth gains are single LRW runs, and the LRW SOTA margin is 0.1.
sensor: Lip crop 112x112; mel-spectrogram in training only
task: Word-level lip reading (LRW, LRW-1000) and sentence-level lip reading (LRS2)
vocabulary: 500 English words; 1,000 Mandarin words; open-vocabulary sentences
speaker: Benchmark splits; speaker overlap not stated
key_result: LRW 88.5%, LRW-1000 53.82%, LRS2 44.5% WER without LM
limitations: Single runs; homophene analysis without per-word counts; no LRW-1000 no-memory baseline

title: EarCommand: "Hearing" Your Silent Speech Commands In Ear
authors: Yincheng Jin; Yang Gao; Xuhai Xu; Seokmin Choi; Jiyang Li; Feng Liu; Zhengxiong Li; Zhanpeng Jin
summary: Earphone SSI senses ear-canal deformation with inaudible in-ear echoes to recognize silently mouthed commands; abstract reports 10.02% WER on 32 word commands and 12.33% on 25 sentence commands.
sensor: Earbud with inward-facing speaker and microphone (near-ultrasound echoes in ear canal)
speaker: Not stated
key_result: WER 10.02% (word commands), 12.33% (sentence commands)
limitations: Reviewed from abstract and press only; closed command sets; participant count and calibration details unverified.

title: FastLTS: Non-Autoregressive End-to-End Unconstrained Lip-to-Speech Synthesis
venue: Proceedings of the 30th ACM International Conference on Multimedia (MM '22)
authors: Yongqi Wang; Zhou Zhao
summary: Parallel decoder, learned-feature GAN generator and transformer front end (M06) are standard; 9.14x mel speedup is real, but evaluation (M12) drops the STOI/ESTOI its Lip2Wav baseline reported.
sensor: Silent talking-face video
speaker: Speaker-dependent: 3 Lip2Wav speakers, 3 unnamed GRID speakers
key_result: MOS above Lip2Wav on most Lip2Wav rows; GRID PESQ 1.939; 9.14x mel-level speedup over Lip2Wav at 3 s
limitations: Benchmark corpora only with three speakers per dataset slice; no in-the-wild user study or live camera-to-audio latency test.

title: Generalizable spelling using a speech neuroprosthesis in an individual with severe limb and vocal paralysis
authors: Sean L. Metzger; Jessie R. Liu; David A. Moses; Maximilian E. Dougherty; Margaret P. Seaton; Kaylo T. Littlejohn; Josh Chartier; Gopala K. Anumanchipalli; Adelyn Tu-Chan; Karunesh Ganguly; Edward F. Chang
summary: Silent NATO code-word spelling (M04), closed-lexicon beam search (M07) and a hand-squeeze stop (M09) are standard; one participant, and >9,000 words only offline.
sensor: 128-channel ECoG over sensorimotor cortex
task: Sentence spelling from silently attempted NATO code words; hand squeeze ends the sentence
speaker: One participant with anarthria and severe limb paralysis
mode: Online (copy typing, conversation) and offline simulation
key_result: Median 6.13% CER, 10.53% WER, 29.41 characters per minute (copy typing, 1,152 words)
limitations: One participant; closed lexicon with out-of-vocabulary exclusions; larger vocabularies offline only; no independent use

title: Imagined speech can be decoded from low- and cross-frequency intracranial EEG features
authors: Timothée Proix; Jaime Delgado Saa; Andy Christen; Stephanie Martin; Brian N. Pasley; Robert T. Knight; Xing Tian; David Poeppel; Werner K. Doyle; Orrin Devinsky; Luc H. Arnal; Pierre Mégevand; Anne-Lise Giraud
summary: Adds low-frequency power (precedent: Pei 2011, Ikeda 2014) and phase-amplitude coupling (new) to imagined-speech ECoG decoding (M06); CFC effect unshown: 12 of 144 uncorrected tests.
sensor: Clinical ECoG, 13 patients
task: Binary classification of grouped imagined and overt words or syllables
vocabulary: 6 English words; 12 French or German words; 3 syllables
speaker: 13 epilepsy patients (8 in binary decoding)
key_result: Imagined CFC: 12 participant-representation pairs above per-participant chance, median balanced accuracy 0.60
limitations: Offline, binary, uncorrected significance across bands and CFC combinations, trial-level CV within participant

title: Improved Processing of Ultrasound Tongue Videos by Combining ConvLSTM and 3D Convolutional Networks
authors: Amin Honarmandi Shandiz; László Tóth
summary: ConvLSTM top layer (M06) is standard: new to ultrasound-to-speech, but a 2.1% MSE edge over BiLSTM, one speaker, one run; later work dropped it. No MCD or listener test (M12 behind).
sensor: Micro ultrasound tongue probe with headset, plus microphone
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: MSE ~0.276, mean R2 ~0.73 on mel-spectrogram regression
limitations: Single-speaker dataset with no perceptual intelligibility testing, cross-speaker evaluation, or real-time tests.

title: Learning Audio-Visual Speech Representation by Masked Multimodal Cluster Prediction
authors: Bowen Shi; Wei-Ning Hsu; Kushal Lakhotia; Abdelrahman Mohamed
summary: AV-HuBERT's masked audio-visual cluster pre-training (M03) was a large step past distillation, but its LRS3 gains lack repeated runs and later work beats it at matched budgets.
sensor: Camera and microphone (audio-visual video; video-only at lipreading inference)
speaker: Speaker-independent
key_result: 32.5% WER (30 h labels), 26.9% WER (433 h + self-training) on LRS3 lipreading
limitations: Vocalized English TED-style video only; no silent-articulation, real-time or on-device evaluation; heavy pretraining compute.

title: Lip-to-Speech Synthesis for Arbitrary Speakers in the Wild
venue: Proceedings of the 30th ACM International Conference on Multimedia (MM '22)
authors: Sindhu B Hegde; K R Prajwal; Rudrabha Mukhopadhyay; Vinay P Namboodiri; C. V. Jawahar
summary: VAE-GAN lip-to-speech with a reference-audio voice: a standard design whose gains are in distribution and sync metrics; no WER is reported, behind its own lineage on evaluation.
sensor: Silent lip/face video plus a one-second reference-audio clip for the voice
speaker: Speaker-independent
key_result: LRS2 FDSD 1.273 (lip-to-text plus TTS 0.984) and LSE-C 2.507; PESQ/STOI 0.60/0.34, below the sequence-to-sequence baseline (0.97/0.43); no WER reported
limitations: No word error rate on the output; listener test on 15 LRS2 samples; voice reference source at test not stated; SED not shown to be independent of the voice-loss identity network; single runs; struggles with non-frontal faces and produces wrong words.

title: Movement Detection of Tongue and Related Body Parts Using IR-UWB Radar
authors: Sunghwa Lee; Younghoon Shin
summary: Chin-aimed radar and an envelope + GMM-HMM front end are standard; the binary rest-vs-touch task shows some closed-mouth movement, not tongue-specific sensing.
sensor: IR-UWB radar with sinuous antennas and dielectric lens
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: >=90% accuracy per participant, 2 tongue states, 4 participants
limitations: Only two states, four participants, manual trial boundaries, stationary lab setup; no continuous speech, unseen-user, or vocabulary-level tests.

title: Robust Self-Supervised Audio-Visual Speech Recognition
authors: Bowen Shi; Wei-Ning Hsu; Abdelrahman Mohamed
summary: Noise-augmented self-supervised AVSR training (M03) was new in 2022 but rests on one test set with no run count; the 49.6% babble gain mixes data and model size with pre-training.
sensor: Lip-region video and one microphone
task: Sentence-level audio-visual speech recognition in added noise (LRS3)
speaker: LRS3 test speakers; split counts not stated
key_result: LRS3 AVSR WER 1.4% clean (433 h labels) and 14.1% mean babble WER at -10 to 10 dB with 30 h labels
limitations: No run count, seeds or test-set interval; one test set; headline comparison mixes unlabelled data and model size with label budget

title: Sequence-to-Sequence Voice Reconstruction for Silent Speech in a Tonal Language
authors: Huiyan Li; Haohong Lin; You Wang; Hengyang Wang; Ming Zhang; Han Gao; Qing Ai; Zhiyuan Luo; Guang Li
summary: Duration-regulated seq2seq with toneme loss voices silent Mandarin EMG; gains rest on the auxiliary loss, not the architecture, and prompt grouping in the utterance split is unreported.
sensor: Five facial wet Ag/AgCl sEMG channels, 2000 Hz
speaker: Speaker-dependent (six speakers, one model each)
key_result: 21.99% objective ASR CER (MASR, mean of six speakers), stated as 24.63% better than the Gaddy-Klein 2020 baseline (absolute or relative not stated); 6.41% listener CER; single runs, utterance-level split with five repetitions per prompt and no stated prompt grouping
limitations: Gain confounded by an auxiliary toneme loss the baseline lacks; length regulator never ablated and the model fails without the toneme loss; tone changes CER by +6.51 in one run; units of Table VI changes unstated; prompt grouping in the split not reported; no seeds, significance test or latency; MASR checkpoint unstated.

title: SilentSpeller: Towards mobile, hands-free, silent speech text entry using electropalatography
authors: Naoki Kimura; Tan Gemicioglu; Jonathan Womack; Yuhui Zhao; Richard Li; Abdelkareem Bedri; Zixiong Su; Alex Olwal; Jun Rekimoto; Thad Starner
summary: SilentSpeller enables silent spelling text entry with an in-mouth electropalatography retainer, reaching 37 wpm at 87% accuracy in live entry and comparable accuracy while walking.
sensor: SmartPalate retainer, 124 capacitive electrodes (EPG)
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: Live entry 37 wpm at 87% accuracy (best 53 wpm, 91%); 92% word accuracy offline
limitations: Strongly user-dependent; requires an obtrusive custom-fitted in-mouth retainer; offline tuning used only two main participants.

title: Sub-word Level Lip Reading With Visual Attention
venue: Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR)
authors: K. R. Prajwal; Triantafyllos Afouras; Andrew Zisserman
summary: Attention pooling of the lip map (M06) was ahead in 2021 but not the route to later SOTA; WordPiece output (M08) was preceded by BPE in 2020; the SOTA table mixes data budgets.
sensor: Camera (face/lip video of voiced speech, audio unused)
speaker: Not stated
key_result: 22.6% WER on LRS2, 30.7% on LRS3 (extended training); 28.9%/40.6% public data only
limitations: Camera-only lip reading rather than articulatory SSI; offline benchmark results only, with no live silent dictation, latency, privacy or in-the-wild evaluation.

title: SVTS: Scalable Video-to-Speech Synthesis
authors: Rodrigo Mira; Alexandros Haliassos; Stavros Petridis; Björn W. Schuller; Maja Pantic
summary: Conformer mel predictor plus pretrained vocoder (M06) and data scaling (M03) are standard; GRID/LRW gains hold, but later tests put SVTS at 78-82% WER on LRS3.
sensor: Camera (lip video)
speaker: Both
key_result: WER 2.36% on GRID seen speakers and 13.40% on LRW; no LRS3 WER reported (later tests measure 82.4% and 78.0% on LRS3).
limitations: No listener test or LRS3 WER; single runs; model size and data scaled together; LRW speaker embedding from the test clip's audio.

title: Towards Neural Decoding of Imagined Speech based on Spoken Speech
authors: Seo-Hyun Lee; Young-Eun Lee; Soowon Kim; Byung-Kwan Ko; Seong-Whan Lee
summary: Spoken-to-imagined EEG transfer (M04) is the standard overt-to-covert design; 26.8% vs 30.5% on 5 classes, no chance level, and "comparable" rests on a non-significant omnibus test.
sensor: 64-channel active-electrode EEG cap (10-10 system)
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: 26.8% (spoken-trained, tested on imagined speech) vs 30.5% (imagined-trained 10-fold CV), 5 classes, 7 subjects; omnibus p = 0.0983; no chance level.
limitations: Standard transfer design; transfer below baseline in 5 of 7 subjects; omnibus non-significance read as comparable; no chance level, trial counts or session arrangement; full-trial transfer is nearly equal for imagined speech and visual imagery.

title: VCVTS: Multi-Speaker Video-to-Speech Synthesis via Cross-Modal Knowledge Transfer from Voice Conversion
authors: Disong Wang; Shan Yang; Dan Su; Xunying Liu; Dong Yu; Helen Meng
summary: VCVTS's unit targets, speech-trained decoder and F0 predictor (M02, M03, M06) came early but are untested by ablation: standard. No WER, unlike its baselines: evaluation (M12) behind.
sensor: Silent lip video plus reference speech
speaker: Both
key_result: GRID unseen speakers (Griffin-Lim): STOI 0.582 vs 0.419 for Lip2Wav; no WER
limitations: Large seen/unseen speaker gap and vocoder-dependent quality; offline benchmarks only, requires reference speech, not validated interactively.

title: VisageSynTalk: Unseen Speaker Video-to-Speech Synthesis via Speech-Visage Feature Selection
authors: Joanna Hong; Minsu Kim; Yong Man Ro
summary: VisageSynTalk disentangles speech content and visage (identity) features for video-to-speech synthesis, yielding robust results for unseen speakers on benchmarks.
sensor: Talking-face video
speaker: Both
key_result: Not reported
limitations: Offline benchmarks only with a small MOS study (20 GRID samples, 16 raters); needs clean aligned video, no robustness to pose or occlusion.

title: Visual Speech Recognition for Multiple Languages in the Wild
authors: Pingchuan Ma; Stavros Petridis; Maja Pantic
summary: Joint distillation losses are a standard idea worth 1.5-2.0 LRS3 points, less than recipe and masking; LRS3 31.5% trails 16.9% from public data; 4 of 6 languages lack external baselines.
sensor: Camera (face/lip video)
vocabulary: Open vocabulary; English, Mandarin, Spanish, Italian, Portuguese, French
speaker: Speaker-independent
key_result: 25.5% WER LRS2, 31.5% WER LRS3, 8.0% CER CMLR (best of ten runs)
limitations: Vocalized in-the-wild video only; silent speech untested; small non-English test sets and offline evaluation.

title: VisualTTS: TTS with Accurate Lip-Speech Synchronization for Automatic Voice Over
authors: Junchen Lu; Berrak Sisman; Rui Liu; Mingyang Zhang; Haizhou Li
summary: VisualTTS conditions TTS on silent lip video to improve lip-speech synchronization for automatic voice-over, evaluated on the scripted GRID corpus.
sensor: Mono video camera (lip region) plus text script
speaker: Not stated
key_result: LSE-C 5.87, LSE-D 8.45, MOS 4.17 on GRID test set
limitations: Restricted to scripted GRID data with paired text; no unseen speakers, spontaneous speech, or real-time tests; does not decode silent speech.

title: Advances and Challenges in Deep Lip Reading
authors: Marzieh Oghbaie; Arian Sabaghi; Kooshan Hashemifard; Mohammad Akbari
summary: Survey of deep lip reading covering datasets, pipeline modules, challenges and evaluation metrics; contributes no new model or experiments.
sensor: Video (lip/face)
speaker: Not stated
key_result: Not reported
limitations: Literature synthesis only, with no original experiments or deployment evaluation.

title: An Improved Model for Voicing Silent Speech
venue: Proceedings of the 59th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics and the 11th International Joint Conference on Natural Language Processing (Volume 2: Short Papers)
authors: David Gaddy; Dan Klein
summary: Conv-plus-Transformer EMG encoder (M06) is reused by the 2026 state of the art; the phoneme loss (M02) follows 2018 ultrasound work. Single runs; ablations explain 16.3 of 25.8 points.
sensor: Facial surface EMG electrodes
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: 42.2% automatic WER (DeepSpeech) from 68.0%, single runs; 32.3% mean human WER from two listeners on 40 samples; a later rerun of the model scores 25.74% under Whisper; one speaker, open vocabulary
limitations: One speaker; no seeds or reruns; ablations account for 16.3 of the 25.8-point gain only if effects add, while alignment and batching changes are not ablated; DeepSpeech version and scorer unstated; test split inherited from 2020 with no held-out session; last-epoch checkpoint; human check of 40 samples by two listeners 7.6 points apart.

title: Convolutional Neural Network-Based Age Estimation Using B-Mode Ultrasound Tongue Image
authors: Kele Xu; Tamás Gábor Csapó; Ming Feng
summary: Age output from tongue ultrasound (M08) is new but unproven: the random frame split shares children between training and validation (M12), so speaker identity can explain the gain.
sensor: B-mode ultrasound tongue images
speaker: 58 UXTD and 20 UPX children; grouping of children across the split not stated
key_result: Validation MSE 2.03 on UXTD (baseline 3.64); 4.87 on UPX (baseline 5.35)
limitations: Children not held out (random frame split), so speaker identity can explain the result; validation data also used for selection; MAE/MSE label conflict; no test set or seeds; therapy use not tested.

title: EMA2S: An End-to-End Multimodal Articulatory-to-Speech System
venue: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
authors: Yu-Wen Chen; Kuo-Hsuan Hung; Shang-Yi Chuang; Jonathan Sherman; Wen-Chin Huang; Xugang Lu; Yu Tsao
summary: Speech-latent target (M02) has a 2017 precedent and small, mixed single-run gains; spectrogram-loss-only end-to-end loses to WORLD (M06); a preference test replaces listener transcription (M12).
sensor: EMA with nine sensors (lips, jaw, tongue)
speaker: Not stated
key_result: Not reported
limitations: Small dataset (three speakers, 354 utterances each), small listening test, no cross-speaker testing, and intrusive lab-grade EMA hardware.

title: End-to-End Audio-Visual Speech Recognition with Conformers
venue: IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech and Signal Processing (ICASSP)
authors: Pingchuan Ma; Stavros Petridis; Maja Pantic
summary: Conformer back-end on raw inputs (M06) and Transformer LM (M07) are standard: raw-input AVSR predates it, and the Conformer gain is one unrepeated step confounded with a decoder swap.
sensor: 88x88 grayscale mouth crop; raw 16 kHz waveform
task: Sentence-level audio-only, visual-only and audio-visual speech recognition (LRS2, LRS3)
speaker: Speaker-independent LRS3 v0.4; LRS3 v0.0 with speaker overlap; LRS2 not stated
key_result: LRS3 v0.4 WER 43.3% visual-only, 2.3% audio-only and audio-visual; LRS2 37.9% visual-only, 3.7% audio-visual
limitations: Single runs; the Conformer gain is one ablation step that also changes the decoder; comparison rows mix data budgets and LRS3 test versions

title: End-to-End Silent Speech Recognition with Acoustic Sensing
authors: Jian Luo; Jianzong Wang; Ning Cheng; Guilin Jiang; Jing Xiao
summary: Standard on sensing and decoding: phone-sonar phase features and an attention decoder work on 54 mouthed sentences of 29 words; the cross-user claim rests on tuning data that include the test users.
sensor: Smartphone speaker and microphone, 8 near-ultrasonic carriers (17–23 kHz), I/Q phase features
task: Silent sentence recognition from lip movements (active acoustic sensing)
vocabulary: 54 fixed Standard Chinese sentences built from 29 words
speaker: 10 volunteers; random split, leave-one-domain-out (user and position) and leave-one-sentence-out tests
session: 5 sessions per volunteer on different days; split across sessions not stated
key_result: WER 2.6% (random split), 8.4% (leave-one-domain-out), 8.1% (leave-one-sentence-out); attention beats CTC by 0.7 to 2.1 points.
limitations: Closed 29-word vocabulary; hyperparameters tuned on a random split that includes held-out users; one run per test, no seeds; phase gain shown in one ablation; no latency or power figures.

title: High-performance brain-to-text communication via handwriting
authors: Francis R. Willett; Donald T. Avansino; Leigh R. Hochberg; Jaimie M. Henderson; Krishna V. Shenoy
summary: Attempted handwriting (M04) is a new text-entry action, but one participant; label timing (M02) and decoder (M06) are standard; the >99% headline relies on an offline language model.
sensor: Two intracortical microelectrode arrays in hand-knob precentral gyrus
task: Attempted handwriting decoded to text in real time (copy typing and free typing)
vocabulary: 31 characters (lowercase letters and punctuation); offline 50,000-word bigram language model
speaker: Participant-dependent (one participant, T5)
key_result: 90 characters per minute at 5.4% raw CER (plateau); five-day raw CER 5.9%, WER 25.1%; offline LM 0.89% CER, 3.4% WER; free typing 73.8 characters per minute at 8.54% CER
limitations: Single participant; no backspace or editing; language model only offline; calibration-reduction and unsupervised retraining results offline.

title: Improving Neural Silent Speech Interface Models by Adversarial Training
authors: Amin Honarmandi Shandiz; László Tóth; Gábor Gosztolya; Alexandra Markó; Tamás Gábor Csapó
summary: Standard on the adversarial loss (M02): it predates the paper in video-to-speech and its gains are small, with no variance reported; behind on evaluation (M12): no listening test.
sensor: Midsagittal ultrasound tongue imaging, Articulate Instruments Micro, 82 fps, resized to 64x128
task: Ultrasound-to-mel-spectrogram mapping with a 3D CNN, WaveGlow synthesis; MSE-only versus MSE plus Patch-GAN adversarial loss
vocabulary: Read sentences (Hungarian; English TaL1), vocalized; vocabulary not stated
speaker: One speaker per corpus (Hungarian female; TaL1 English); train and test from the same speaker
session: Not stated; split procedure not given (counts only), no held-out session reported
key_result: Test STOI 0.7050 to 0.7067 (Hungarian) and 0.612 to 0.623 (English); MCD 4.627 to 4.558 and 3.38 to 3.229 dB; no variance reported, no listening test.
limitations: No repeated runs or variance reported; MSE-only baseline also loses on MSE; output window changed for the GAN runs; loss weights selected on an unstated set; objective metrics only, including SDR and SI-SDR on vocoded speech; one speaker per corpus.

title: Learning from the Master: Distilling Cross-modal Advanced Knowledge for Lip Reading
venue: IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR)
authors: Sucheng Ren; Yong Du; Jianming Lv; Guoqiang Han; Shengfeng He
summary: Look-ahead audio-visual master (M02) is new for lip reading but shown on one LRS2 run; confidence curriculum (M03) adds 0.1-1.1 WER points; SOTA claim fails on LRW and LRS3.
sensor: Lip-region RGB video at test; paired raw audio used only to train the master and the audio tutor
task: Word-level (LRW) and sentence-level (LRS2, LRS3) lip reading
vocabulary: 500 words (LRW); 40 character symbols for open-vocabulary sentences
speaker: Not stated; benchmark splits
mode: Voiced speech video; video only at test
key_result: LRW 14.3% WER (Ours-TM, Table 2), 11.8% with the MS-TCN backend (Table 6); LRS2 49.2% and LRS3 59.0% WER
limitations: Single runs; LM use not stated; master effect isolated on LRS2 only; comparators with mixed LM settings

title: LiRA: Learning Visual Speech Representations from Audio through Self-supervision
authors: Pingchuan Ma; Rodrigo Mira; Stavros Petridis; Björn W. Schuller; Maja Pantic
summary: LiRA's audio-feature pre-training (M02, M03) is standard: it helps at 1% of labels but adds 0.7 points on LRW and 0.3 on LRS2 with all labels; its lead over other self-supervised work is the backbone.
sensor: dlib-landmark mouth ROI, 96x96, 88x88 crop, 25 fps
task: Self-supervised visual speech representation learning from audio for word- and sentence-level lip reading
speaker: Public LRW and LRS2 test sets; speaker overlap not stated in the paper
key_result: LRW 88.1% (87.4% from scratch); LRS2 VSR WER 38.8% (39.1% from scratch with curriculum); LRW 24.5% against 3.6% at 1% labels
limitations: Single runs without seeds; PASE+ target not compared with other targets; LM partitions and decoding weights not stated

title: Multi-modality Associative Bridging through Memory: Speech Sound Recollected from Face Video
venue: Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision (ICCV)
authors: Minsu Kim; Joanna Hong; Se Jin Park; Yong Man Ro
summary: Audio memory recall (M02) is ahead as a design, but the LRW state-of-the-art claim misses a prior 87.9% model, the edge over distillation is one run, and GRID gains are small.
sensor: Silent face video
task: Lip reading and speech synthesis from video
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: LRW 85.41% (+1.27 over baseline, +0.91 over distillation), below a prior 87.9% single model; LRW-1000 50.82% (+5.89), 2.8 above the best prior model without word boundaries; GRID seen speakers STOI 0.738 vs 0.731 (Lip2Wav), no WER
limitations: Best memory size of an ablation, one run, with no stated validation rule; edge over distillation is one LRW run; LRW state-of-the-art claim misses a prior 87.9% model and the LRW-1000 lead holds only without word boundaries; no GRID no-memory score in the main text; GRID objective scores use Griffin-Lim and the MOS gain comes from WaveNet; no WER; offline only.

title: Neural Speaker Embeddings for Ultrasound-based Silent Speech Interfaces
authors: Amin Honarmandi Shandiz; László Tóth; Gábor Gosztolya; Alexandra Markó; Tamás Gábor Csapó
summary: Standard on embedding conditioning (2.4% relative MSE gain on seen speakers); behind on speaker recognition, which never separates speaker from recording session.
sensor: Midsagittal ultrasound tongue imaging, Articulate Instruments Micro, 82 fps (TaL80 corpus)
task: Speaker recognition from ultrasound (x-vector) and multi-speaker ultrasound-to-mel-spectrum estimation conditioned on it
speaker: x-vector trained on 50 speakers, scored on 31 held-out speakers; SSI trained and tested on the same 31 speakers
session: About one TaL80 recording session per speaker (inferred from corpus totals); speaker and session not separated
key_result: 0.70% 1-NN speaker error on 31 held-out speakers (pooled segments); x-vector input lowers multi-speaker test MSE from 0.669 to 0.653, 2.4% relative, one reported run.
limitations: Speaker recognition not tested across sessions; SSI tested only on seen speakers; single runs without seeds or chance levels; no listening, MCD or intelligibility score for multi-speaker systems.

title: Neuroprosthesis for decoding speech in a paralyzed person with anarthria
authors: David A. Moses; Sean L. Metzger; Jessie R. Liu; Gopala K. Anumanchipalli; Joseph G. Makin; Pengfei F. Sun; Josh Chartier; Maximilian E. Dougherty; Patricia M. Liu; Gary M. Abrams; Adelyn Tu-Chan; Karunesh Ganguly; Edward F. Chang
summary: Sentence decoding from a person who cannot speak holds for 50 words and one participant; the decoder is standard, and an LM restricted to the test vocabulary drives the gain.
sensor: 128-electrode high-density ECoG over sensorimotor cortex
task: Attempted word and sentence decoding to text
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: Median WER 25.6% with LM (60.5% without), 15.2 wpm; isolated words 47.1% (chance 2%)
limitations: Single participant, 50-word vocabulary, strong reliance on the language model, spurious detections, no independent use.

title: Real-time synthesis of imagined speech processes from minimally invasive recordings of neural activity
authors: Miguel Angrick; Maarten C. Ottenhoff; Lorenz Diener; Darius Ivucic; Gabriel Ivucic; Sophocles Goulis; Jeremy Saal; Albert J. Colon; Louis Wagner; Dean J. Krusienski; Pieter L. Kubben; Tanja Schultz; Christian Herff
summary: Closed-loop sEEG word synthesis (M06) and audible-to-imagined transfer (M04) are standard; one participant; imagined output lacks word identification and an imagery control (M12 behind).
sensor: sEEG depth electrodes (119 contacts, 11 shafts)
task: Real-time synthesis of single prompted Dutch words from sEEG; audible training, whispered and imagined closed-loop runs
vocabulary: 250-word phonetically balanced list, 100 words per run
speaker: One participant (epilepsy monitoring)
session: One audible open-loop run and two closed-loop runs
key_result: Closed-loop DTW correlation 0.64 whispered and 0.32 imagined against 0.17 non-speech chance
limitations: One participant; output not intelligible; no word identification test; imagery not separated from prompt reading; null from a separate non-speech session

title: Silent Speech and Emotion Recognition from Vocal Tract Shape Dynamics in Real-Time MRI
authors: Laxmi Pandey; Ahmed Sabbir Arif
summary: LipNet decoder on rtMRI (M06) and new sentence-text output (M08) are standard; one unseen-speaker split without repeats; a shared 460-sentence list likely puts training sentences in the test.
sensor: Real-time MRI scanner (full vocal tract)
speaker: 8 training, 2 held-out test speakers
key_result: PER 40.6%, CER 39.4%, WER 42.1% with the language model on two held-out USC-TIMIT speakers (one split).
limitations: One split without repeats; shared 460-sentence list likely overlaps train and test; audible, not silent, speech; no emotion classifier; language model and PER definition inconsistent.

title: Silent versus modal multi-speaker speech recognition from ultrasound and video
authors: Manuel Sam Ribeiro; Aciel Eshky; Korin Richmond; Steve Renals
summary: Standard on both changed components: modal-to-silent loss and fMLLR were known; later work narrows the absolute gap but not the fMLLR ratio, and adaptation gains rest on single runs.
sensor: Ultrasound tongue imaging and lip video (TaL corpus)
task: Sentence recognition from articulatory images: modal-trained, tested on modal, silent and whispered speech
vocabulary: Read TaL prompts; in-domain bigram LM on a superset of the corpus prompts
speaker: Multi-speaker (82 speakers, test speakers seen in training) and speaker-dependent (TaL1)
session: TaL1: per-session fMLLR; test sessions not stated
key_result: Modal-trained recognition: TaL80 silent WER 70.21 vs modal 39.79 with fMLLR (30.42 points, about 76% higher); unsupervised adaptation adds at most 3.36 silent points and raises modal WER; a later system on TaL narrows the absolute gap to 20.28 points but keeps the fMLLR ratio near 1.75.
limitations: Test speakers are in the training set; single runs with no seeds or significance tests; adaptation is scored on its own adaptation data; LM test-prompt inclusion not stated; correlations of WER with duration and tongue space have no intervals.

title: Speaker disentanglement in video-to-speech conversion
authors: Dan Oneață; Adriana Stan; Horia Cucu
summary: Speaker-conditioned video-to-speech with adversarial identity removal: both standard (gradient reversal on GRID lips dates from 2017); EER uses the training embedding network; one run.
sensor: Camera (silent lip video) plus speaker embedding
speaker: Both
key_result: About 38.9% WER, 11.9% EER (gradient reversal), unseen speaker identity control, GRID
limitations: Closed-vocabulary read GRID speech only; intelligibility-control trade-off worsens on unseen speakers and speaker identity or embedding is required at inference.

title: Speech Synthesis from Text and Ultrasound Tongue Image-based Articulatory Input
authors: Tamás Gábor Csapó; László Tóth; Gábor Gosztolya; Alexandra Markó
summary: Text+ultrasound input to DNN-TTS (M06) is standard: test MCD falls 0.015-0.229 dB on 8 speakers; BAP, voicing worsen on test, F0 correlation improves; no listening test.
sensor: Micro ultrasound system with probe-fixing headset
task: Speech synthesis from text plus ultrasound
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: Test MCD 5.442 (text+ultrasound) vs 5.652 (text-only) vs 7.153 (ultrasound-only), speaker 03mn
limitations: Not a standalone SSI: best system still needs text input; speaker-dependent, limited data, sensitive to probe misalignment, and no listening tests.

title: Voice Activity Detection for Ultrasound-based Silent Speech Interfaces using Convolutional Neural Networks
authors: Amin Honarmandi Shandiz; László Tóth
summary: Frame-wise ultrasound CNN VAD (M06) and audio-VAD labels (M02) are standard; one-speaker file-split test (M12) is behind held-out-speaker VAD work; 85% is 11 points over majority.
sensor: Ultrasound tongue imaging
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: 85.2% test accuracy, F1 0.9, ROC AUC 0.859, single speaker
limitations: Single-speaker data with speech-derived labels; no cross-speaker validation, live test, or robustness to probe shift and new users.

title: 3D Convolutional Neural Networks for Ultrasound-Based Silent Speech Interfaces
venue: Artificial Intelligence and Soft Computing (ICAISC 2020), Lecture Notes in Computer Science 12415
authors: László Tóth; Amin Honarmandi Shandiz
summary: (2+1)D front end (M06) is standard: established in lip reading, ported to ultrasound; a 6.3% MSE edge over CNN+LSTM, one speaker, one run; MSE-only evaluation (M12 behind).
sensor: Micro ultrasound system, 64-element convex transducer, 82 fps
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: Test MSE of 13 standardized vocoder parameters: 3D (2+1)D CNN 0.315 vs retrained CNN+LSTM 0.336, 2D CNN 0.366, FCN 0.400; mean R2 0.683 vs 0.661, 0.633, 0.598; one speaker, single runs
limitations: One Hungarian speaker reading aloud; MSE and R2 of vocoder parameters only, no F0, no listening, intelligibility or ASR test; no seeds or variance; context width not matched across models; CNN+LSTM retrained with changed sizes; no silent articulation or latency.

title: A comparison of oscillatory characteristics in covert speech and speech perception
authors: Jae Moon; Silvia Orlandi; Tom Chau
summary: EEG analysis comparing oscillatory activity in covert speech and speech perception in eight participants; finds stronger low-gamma for covert speech, stronger delta/theta for perception, and theta-gamma coupling.
sensor: EEG cap
vocabulary: Small fixed lexicon of 1-2 syllable words
speaker: Not stated
key_result: Not reported
limitations: Eight-participant study with a small lexicon; no SSI decoder, user study or deployment, and visible participant variability.

title: An Overview of Deep-Learning-Based Audio-Visual Speech Enhancement and Separation
authors: Daniel Michelsanti; Zheng-Hua Tan; Shi-Xiong Zhang; Yong Xu; Meng Yu; Dong Yu; Jesper Jensen
summary: Survey of deep-learning audio-visual speech enhancement and separation, mapping design choices and noting the lack of standardized audio-visual evaluation.
sensor: Microphone and camera (review)
speaker: Not stated
key_result: Not reported
limitations: Not a primary SSI contribution; no new benchmark or unified re-evaluation, and lack of standardized evaluation limits performance comparisons.

title: ASR is all you need: cross-modal distillation for lip reading
venue: IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech and Signal Processing (ICASSP)
authors: Triantafyllos Afouras; Joon Son Chung; Andrew Zisserman
summary: ASR-teacher labels (M02) replaced transcribed-data alignment targets; standard: LRS2 parity holds, but effects differ across datasets, one WER each, and distillation is not isolated.
sensor: Face video for lip reading; paired audio used only in training
speaker: Not stated
mode: Overt speech; video only at test
key_result: LRS3 WER 61.7% without human transcripts (clean VoxCeleb2 + LRS3 with ASR labels); 59.8% after ground-truth fine-tuning
limitations: Single runs; no CTC-on-ASR-labels control; ASR-filtered unlabelled subset; comparator decoders not stated

title: Audio-Visual Recognition of Overlapped Speech for the LRS2 Dataset
venue: IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech and Signal Processing (ICASSP)
authors: Jianwei Yu; Shi-Xiong Zhang; Jian Wu; Shahram Ghorbani; Bo Wu; Shiyin Kang; Shansong Liu; Xunying Liu; Helen Meng; Dong Yu
summary: Gated AV fusion for overlapped speech (M06) is standard: AV-driven fusion weights (2006) and mixture recognition with lips (2016) came first; 15.20% to 10.31% WER, no seeds; test interferers unstated.
sensor: Single-channel microphone audio and target-speaker lip video (112x112 mouth ROI, upsampled to 100 fps)
task: Recognition of the target speaker in simulated two-talker LRS2 mixtures; clean LRS2 lip reading, ASR and AVSR
speaker: Many speakers (LRS2 splits, no speaker labels)
key_result: Two-talker LRS2 mixtures: 10.31% average WER with audio-visual gating plus concatenation against 15.20% with feature concatenation and 10.92% for the best pipelined system; clean LRS2 5.93% audio-visual WER
limitations: No seeds or variance; test-interferer source and mixture count not stated; no clean test for the overlap systems; gated systems have more layers than the concatenation baseline (24 vs 15); Table 1 comparators without their language model.

title: Brain2Char: a deep architecture for decoding text from brain recordings
authors: Pengfei Sun; Gopala K. Anumanchipalli; Edward F. Chang
summary: Character CTC decoding from ECoG; all changes are standard. The 7.0-10.6% WER relies on repeated sentences, as the authors concede, and unseen sentences average 80% WER.
sensor: Implanted ECoG grids (16x16, 16x8) on speech cortex
task: Sentence-level text decoding from brain signals
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: WER 7.0-10.6% for three participants on repeated sentences (1200-1900 word vocabularies); unseen sentences average 80% WER
limitations: Invasive implant, per-subject calibration, four participants, best results rely on repeated sentences, no cross-subject transfer.

title: Can We Read Speech Beyond the Lips? Rethinking RoI Selection for Deep Visual Speech Recognition
venue: 2020 15th IEEE International Conference on Automatic Face and Gesture Recognition (FG 2020)
authors: Yuanhang Zhang; Shuang Yang; Jingyun Xiao; Shiguang Shan; Xilin Chen
summary: Face Cutout (M03) is ahead but untested on mouth crops; the face RoI (M05) is standard, as face and mouth were compared before; the GRID 2.9% claim relies on an LM.
sensor: Aligned whole face; upper face and cheeks as probes
task: Word-level (LRW, LRW-1000) and sentence-level (GRID) visual speech recognition
speaker: LRW/LRW-1000 official splits (speaker overlap not stated); GRID overlapped speakers
key_result: Face + Cutout: LRW 85.02%, LRW-1000 45.24%, GRID 2.9% WER (5-gram character LM)
limitations: Single runs; no mouth-plus-Cutout control; LRW-1000 initialised from LRW; GRID overlapped speakers with LM

title: Continuous Silent Speech Recognition using EEG
authors: Gautam Krishna; Co Tran; Mason Carnahan; Ahmed H Tewfik
summary: Standard on silent reading (M04) and CTC decoding (M06); 83% WER on 30 sentences repeated in training, with an undisclosed 4-gram LM and no chance baseline, does not show EEG decoding.
sensor: 31-channel wet scalp EEG (32-electrode cap incl. ground, 10-20 placement), 1000 Hz; five statistical features per channel at 100 Hz, KPCA to 20 dimensions
task: Continuous character-level CTC recognition of silently read sentences from EEG, with beam search and an external 4-gram language model
vocabulary: First 30 USC-TIMIT sentences; test subsets of 5 to 30 unique sentences, all repeated in training
speaker: Four male participants (three non-native English speakers); one train-on-three, test-on-fourth run
session: Three repetitions of the 30 sentences per participant; session boundaries not stated
key_result: 83.34% WER on 72 test recordings covering all 30 sentences (74.86% to 84.08% across subsets); 92.55% WER on a held-out subject.
limitations: Test sentences repeat training sentences; language-model corpus and weight not reported; no chance or shuffled-label baseline; single runs without seeds; sentence displayed on screen, so reading and inner speech are not separated.

title: Decoding Imagined and Spoken Phrases From Non-invasive Neural (MEG) Signals
authors: Debadatta Dash; Paul Ferrari; Jun Wang
summary: Scalogram CNNs (M06) and ImageNet weights (M03) were new for imagined speech but standard: effects not isolated; 93% imagination sits on a 43.77% pre-stimulus floor (Table 1).
sensor: 196 of 204 gradiometers, Elekta MEG, 1 kHz
speaker: Not stated

title: Decoding spoken English from intracortical electrode arrays in dorsal precentral gyrus
authors: Guy H. Wilson; Sergey D. Stavisky; Francis R. Willett; Donald T. Avansino; Jessica N. Kelemen; Leigh R. Hochberg; Jaimie M. Henderson; Shaul Druckmann; Krishna V. Shenoy
summary: 39-phoneme decoding from dorsal Utah arrays (M06) and overt-speech confound controls (M12) are standard: both have read priors, T5 alone carries them, and folds share words.
sensor: Two 96-electrode Utah arrays per participant in dorsal precentral gyrus (hand knob); HLFP and threshold crossings
task: Offline classification of 39 phonemes within prompted overt words; Brain-to-Speech unit-selection synthesis
speaker: Two BrainGate2 participants (T5, T11), within-participant
key_result: 39-phoneme accuracy 29.3% (logistic regression) and 33.9% (RNN) in T5; 25.8% after acoustic decontamination
limitations: Utterance-level folds share words; confound controls in T5 only; offline, overt speech, no online test

title: Digital Voicing of Silent Speech
venue: Proceedings of the 2020 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing (EMNLP)
authors: David Gaddy; Dan Klein
summary: Silent-EMG target transfer (M02) extends a 2016 DTW recipe; the open corpus scored by WER (M12) became the shared test bed. Headline 94% gain is closed-vocabulary, 20 clips, one evaluator.
sensor: Facial and throat surface EMG electrodes
vocabulary: Closed dates/times set; open vocabulary of 9828 words
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: 3.6% human WER closed vocabulary; 74.8% human WER open vocabulary
limitations: Speaker-dependent with substantial data collection; open-vocabulary WER remains high and all results come from the authors' own data setup.

title: Discriminative Multi-modality Speech Recognition
venue: Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR)
authors: Bo Xu; Cheng Lu; Yandong Guo; Jacob Wang
summary: Enhance-then-AV-recognise (M06) is standard: video used twice predates it (2002, 2013); LRS3 0 dB WER 41.1% to 25.5%, but one run, a clean-trained AV baseline and copied baselines.
sensor: Microphone audio and lip video (112x112 mouth crop, 25 fps)
task: Audio-visual sentence recognition in babble noise (LRS3-TED); word-level lip reading (LRW)
vocabulary: Open vocabulary, 41 output characters; LRW 500 words
speaker: Many speakers (benchmark splits); speaker overlap not stated
key_result: LRS3, 0 dB babble: 25.5% WER with enhancement plus audio-visual recognition (T-EG-s2s), against 41.1% audio-visual without enhancement; LRW 84.8% word accuracy
limitations: One run per system; audio-visual baseline described as trained on clean magnitudes; several baseline cells are published values of Afouras et al. obtained with other training data and babble; no P3D or EleAtt-GRU ablation.

title: Hearing Lips: Improving Lip Reading by Distilling Speech Recognizers
venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence
authors: Ya Zhao; Rui Xu; Xinchao Wang; Peng Hou; Haihong Tang; Mingli Song
summary: Recognizer-to-lip-reader distillation (M02) is ahead of the prior record and repeats over two datasets and three teachers; the audio rationale is untested and the LRS2 state-of-the-art claim fails.
sensor: Mouth-region video; paired audio used only to train the speech-recognizer teacher
task: Sentence-level lip reading (visual speech recognition), Mandarin and English
vocabulary: Open vocabulary; 1,779 Chinese characters (CMLR) or 26 English letters (LRS2)
speaker: Not stated; CMLR split is random over eleven hosts
session: Not stated; LRS2 split by broadcast date
mode: Overt speech; muted video at test
key_result: CMLR CER 31.27% (WAS 38.93%); LRS2 CER 45.53% and WER 65.29% (WAS 48.28% and 68.19%)
limitations: Single runs; no same-modality teacher control; LM use not stated; LRS2 comparators better on WER

title: Learning Individual Speaking Styles for Accurate Lip to Speech Synthesis
venue: 2020 IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR)
authors: K R Prajwal; Rudrabha Mukhopadhyay; Vinay P. Namboodiri; C V Jawahar
summary: Lip2Wav's per-speaker natural corpus (M03) is ahead; its attention decoder (M06) is standard, since LipSound had one in 2019; two Table 2 baseline WERs match another recognizer's values.
sensor: Face crop 48x48
task: Single-speaker lip-to-speech synthesis (silent face video to mel spectrogram and waveform)
vocabulary: Open vocabulary, more than 5,000 words per Lip2Wav speaker; GRID 56-token grammar; TCD-TIMIT sentences; LRW 500 words
speaker: Speaker-dependent: one model per speaker (5 Lip2Wav speakers, 4 GRID speakers, TCD-TIMIT lip speakers); LRW multi-speaker baseline
session: Video-disjoint train and test splits within each Lip2Wav speaker
mode: Voiced speech video with audio removed at test, offline
key_result: Lip2Wav STOI 0.28-0.45 across the five speakers against at most 0.251 for the two baselines; GRID WER 14.08% (Google ASR); MOS intelligibility 3.04 and naturalness 3.63
limitations: Single runs without seeds; two GRID baseline WERs match values from another recognizer; ablations on one speaker; no WER on Lip2Wav; Griffin-Lim waveform

title: Lipreading using Temporal Convolutional Networks
authors: Brais Martinez; Pingchuan Ma; Stavros Petridis; Maja Pantic
summary: Multi-scale TCN (M06) and variable-length cropping (M03) are standard: head and augmentation are not separated, no run counts, robustness comes from the cropping; 85.3% LRW trails 93.2% today.
sensor: Grayscale 88x88 mouth crop
task: Isolated-word visual lip reading (LRW 500 English words, LRW-1000 1,000 Mandarin classes); audio-visual babble-noise test
speaker: More than 1,000 BBC speakers (LRW); speaker overlap across splits not stated
key_result: LRW 85.3% and LRW-1000 41.4% top-1 accuracy; run count not reported
limitations: No fixed-length TCN row, so back end and augmentation are not separated; robustness from the cropping augmentation; no run count; noise test corpus unnamed

title: Machine translation of cortical activity to text with an encoder-decoder framework
authors: Joseph G. Makin; David A. Moses; Edward F. Chang
summary: Word-level ECoG encoder-decoder; all changed components standard. 3% WER is on repeats of 50 sentences; unseen sentences and participants were never tested.
sensor: Clinical ECoG, ~250 electrodes
task: Overt reading of prompted sentences (MOCHA-TIMIT; picture descriptions)
speaker: Four epilepsy-monitoring participants; per-participant models with cross-participant transfer
key_result: About 3% WER on held-out repeats of MOCHA-1 (example participant); about 33% for a phoneme-HMM sentence classifier
limitations: No unseen-sentence or held-out-participant test; training needs speech audio for the MFCC target; no seeds

title: Silent Speech Interfaces for Speech Restoration: A Review
authors: Jose A. Gonzalez-Lopez; Alejandro Gomez-Alanis; Juan M. Martin-Donas; Jose L. Perez-Cordoba; Angel M. Gomez
summary: Review of SSI modalities for speech restoration, focusing on deployment bottlenecks such as latency, scarce patient data and modality trade-offs; cites ideal latency of about 50 ms, acceptable up to 100 ms.
sensor: Multimodal biosignal and articulator sensors (review)
speaker: Not stated
key_result: Not reported
limitations: A review that synthesizes uneven prior results without a unified benchmark and does not itself resolve deployment obstacles.

title: Speech Prediction in Silent Videos using Variational Autoencoders
authors: Ravindra Yadav; Ashish Sardana; Vinay P Namboodiri; Rajesh M Hegde
summary: Variational autoencoder model for speech synthesis from silent lip video that models one-to-many ambiguity; on GRID reports STOI 0.724, ESTOI 0.540 and PESQ 1.932, leading Lip2Wav on ESTOI and PESQ.
sensor: Camera (silent lip video)
speaker: Not stated
key_result: STOI 0.724, ESTOI 0.540, PESQ 1.932 on GRID
limitations: Limited to the GRID benchmark with Griffin-Lim waveform recovery; no speaker-independent, open-world or real-time evaluation.

title: Ultra2Speech - A Deep Learning Framework for Formant Frequency Estimation and Tracking from Ultrasound Tongue Images
authors: Pramit Saha; Yadong Liu; Bryan Gick; Sidney Fels
summary: Formant target and hybrid front end (M06) are standard; evaluation (M12) is behind: random one-second clip split of one speaker, where earlier ultrasound work held out whole utterances.
sensor: Ultrasound probe (tongue images)
speaker: Not stated
key_result: Mean R2 99.96 on joint f1-f2 prediction vs 90.01 baseline
limitations: Focuses on formant tracking and vowel trajectories rather than full speech reconstruction; single collected dataset, no cross-speaker or real-time device evaluation.

title: Vocoder-Based Speech Synthesis from Silent Videos
authors: Daniel Michelsanti; Olga Slizovskaia; Gloria Haro; Emilia Gómez; Zheng-Hua Tan; Jesper Jensen
summary: WORLD features (M06) beat the 2019 GAN on seen GRID speakers; on unseen ones PESQ ties and ESTOI is higher. The CTC text loss (M02) adds under 0.015 ESTOI; the WER is the text head's.
sensor: Camera (silent frontal face/mouth video)
speaker: Both
key_result: Seen GRID speakers: PESQ 1.90, ESTOI 0.455 against 0.329 for the 2019 GAN; unseen speakers: ESTOI 0.227 against 0.198 with PESQ tied (1.23 against 1.24). WER 15.1% (seen) and 51.6% (unseen) is from the CTC text head, not ASR on the speech.
limitations: GRID only, one run per configuration with the checkpoint chosen by PESQ; text loss adds under 0.015 ESTOI; no ASR on the synthesized speech, no chance level, and the real-time claim has no latency figure.

title: A Cascade Sequence-to-Sequence Model for Chinese Mandarin Lip Reading
venue: Proceedings of the ACM Multimedia Asia (MMAsia '19)
authors: Ya Zhao; Rui Xu; Mingli Song
summary: Explicit tone stage (M06) is new in Mandarin lip reading but standard: no repeated runs, and its 1.59-point CER margin bundles tone with video attention; tone without video is worse (42.23%).
sensor: Broadcast video, 64x128 grayscale lip crops
task: Sentence-level Mandarin lip reading (video to Chinese characters)
speaker: 11 news hosts, shared across train and test
session: Broadcasts June 2009 to June 2018; random 7:1:2 split
key_result: 32.48% CER on CMLR vs 34.07% for a re-implemented LipCH-Net sharing its first stage (no repeated runs)
limitations: Speaker-overlapping split; ASR labels with no reported check; no seeds; tone margin bundled with video attention; partition behind Table 3 not named

title: A Novel Task-Oriented Text Corpus in Silent Speech Recognition and its Natural Language Generation Construction Method
authors: Dong Cao; Dongdong Zhang; HaiBo Chen
summary: Proposes a task-oriented text corpus and a hybrid natural language generation method for building EEG silent speech recognition datasets; claims gains over template and neural NLG but gives no numeric benchmark.
sensor: EEG headset
task: Corpus construction for EEG silent speech recognition
speaker: Not stated
key_result: Not reported
limitations: Does not solve EEG decoding, relies on a narrow domain, and quantitative evidence is too weak to audit the comparative claims.

title: Autoencoder-Based Articulatory-to-Acoustic Mapping for Ultrasound Silent Speech Interfaces
authors: Gábor Gosztolya; Ádám Pintér; László Tóth; Tamás Grósz; Alexandra Markó; Tamás Gábor Csapó
summary: Standard on the encoder: autoencoder features predate it and it is never compared with PCA or DCT; behind on F0, which is copied from the recording, so the listening test is not of a silent system.
sensor: Midsagittal ultrasound tongue imaging, Articulate Instruments Micro, 82 fps, resized to 64x128
task: Ultrasound-to-spectrum estimation (25 MGC-LSP plus gain) for direct synthesis, with autoencoder bottleneck features as input
vocabulary: Read Hungarian sentences (vocalized); vocabulary not stated
speaker: One female speaker; train, development and test from the same speaker
session: Not stated; session-disjoint splits not reported
key_result: Test NMSE 0.534 (pixels, 1 frame) to 0.377 (autoencoder N=256, 13 frames); MUSHRA naturalness 16.58 to 40.98 against 75.16 for vocoded speech, with original F0.
limitations: Only a raw-pixel baseline, no PCA or DCT; F0 copied from the recording; configuration named on development and test scores together; one speaker; no seeds, significance test or intelligibility test.

title: Denoising Convolutional Autoencoder Based B-mode Ultrasound Tongue Image Feature Extraction
authors: Bo Li; Kele Xu; Dawei Feng; Haibo Mi; Huaimin Wang; Jian Zhu
summary: Convolutional denoising AE features (M06) are standard: denoising and CNN features predate it; DCT margin 0.21-0.41 points (2-4 of 1023 words), one speaker, runs unstated.
sensor: Ultrasound tongue imaging (4-8 MHz microconvex probe)
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: SSC WER 6.17% with DCAE features at length 60 against DCT 6.58% at the same length (DCAE 6.24% vs DCT 6.45% at length 30); one speaker, runs not stated
limitations: One speaker, run count not stated, length-mismatched headline comparison; denoising adds 0.05 points; robustness claims untested.

title: Generating Natural, Intelligible Speech From Brain Activity in Motor, Premotor, and Inferior Frontal Cortices
authors: Christian Herff; Lorenz Diener; Miguel Angrick; Emily Mugler; Matthew C. Tate; Matthew A. Goldrick; Dean J. Krusienski; Marc W. Slutzky; Tanja Schultz
summary: Unit selection (M06) and own-voice concatenation (M08) are standard: an EMG design new to ECoG, below the same-data DenseNet; the 4-choice test (M12) on 30 best words; naturalness unmeasured.
sensor: 64-ch 8x8 ECoG, 4 mm; log high gamma, 450 ms context
speaker: Participant-dependent (6 awake-craniotomy patients)
key_result: Mean spectrogram r 0.246 (best 0.574); 66.1% four-choice listener identification (chance 25%) on 30 best words
limitations: Offline, intraoperative, small data; no in-paper decoder comparison; listening stimuli pre-selected; naturalness not measured

title: Lipper: Synthesizing Thy Speech using Multi-View Lipreading
venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence
authors: Yaman Kumar; Rohit Jain; Khwaja Mohd. Salik; Rajiv Ratn Shah; Yifang Yin; Roger Zimmermann
summary: Multi-view input (M05) and LPC/LSP regression (M06) are standard; the view gain shrinks to +2-6% on two held-out speakers. Evaluation (M12) lacks STOI/ESTOI, ASR WER and transcription.
sensor: Up to five synchronized OuluVS2 camera views (0/30/45/60/90 deg)
task: Speech waveform reconstruction from multi-view silent lip video
vocabulary: Ten OuluVS2 phrases; leave-one-phrase-out OOV test
speaker: Speaker-dependent; speaker-independent on two held-out speakers
key_result: PESQ 2.315 for 0+45+60 deg against 2.002 frontal, speaker-dependent (Tables 4, 6); 1.94 / 1.86 on two held-out speakers (Table 10)
limitations: Best view combination chosen on the reported test results; two held-out speakers; PESQ and closed-set phrase identification, no STOI/ESTOI, ASR WER or transcription; delay without hardware.

title: Real-time decoding of question-and-answer speech dialogue using human cortical activity
authors: David A. Moses; Matthew K. Leonard; Joseph G. Makin; Edward F. Chang
summary: Context prior from the decoded question (M07) is ahead, gaining in 3 of 3 participants; HMM decoder (M06) is standard; no online accuracy or latency backs the real-time claim.
sensor: Clinical ECoG, high gamma, 3 patients
task: Closed-set decoding of perceived questions (9) and produced answers (24) in a cued question-and-answer task
speaker: Participant-specific (3 epilepsy patients)
mode: Overt listening and overt speaking; offline simulation of a real-time pipeline
key_result: Best full-system accuracy 61% (answers) and 76% (questions) against chance 7% and 20%; decoded-question context improved answer decoding in all 3 participants
limitations: Offline simulation only; no online accuracy or latency figure; headline values are maxima across 3 participants; question stimuli identical in training and test

title: Recurrent Neural Network Transducer for Audio-Visual Speech Recognition
venue: IEEE Automatic Speech Recognition and Understanding Workshop (ASRU)
authors: Takaki Makino; Hank Liao; Yannis Assael; Brendan Shillingford; Basilio Garcia; Otavio Braga; Olivier Siohan
summary: First neural transducer for audio-visual speech in the ledger, but the LRS3 gain mixes 31k h of data, external-LM baselines and the decoder; one run, one test set: all changes standard.
sensor: Mouth crops, 23 to 30 fps; 16 kHz audio
speaker: Not stated

title: SottoVoce: An Ultrasound Imaging-Based Silent Speech Interaction Using Deep Neural Networks
authors: Naoki Kimura; Michinari Kono; Jun Rekimoto
summary: SottoVoce reconstructs speech audio from under-jaw ultrasound images with two DNNs to control unmodified smart speakers; command success rose from 42.5% to 65.0% with the second network, versus 90.0% for real audio.
sensor: 3.5 MHz convex ultrasound probe under the jaw
task: Speech synthesis from ultrasound for voice-assistant control
vocabulary: ~500 training commands; 4 Alexa commands in end-to-end test
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: 65.0% smart speaker command success (4 commands x5, two networks) vs 90.0% ground-truth audio
limitations: Only two participants, speaker-dependent, tiny end-to-end command set, bulky non-wearable probe, 2.61 s latency, and unassessed ultrasound safety.

title: Spatio-Temporal Fusion based Convolutional Sequence Learning for Lip Reading
venue: IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision (ICCV)
authors: Xingxuan Zhang; Feng Cheng; Shilin Wang
summary: STFM and the convolutional encoder-decoder (M06) are standard: layout-keeping reduction predates it, baselines are weakened; LRW SOTA claim fails; LM use never stated (M07).
sensor: Lip-centred RGB video (112x112 crops)
task: Word-level (LRW) and sentence-level (GRID, LRS2, LRS3) lip reading
vocabulary: 500 words (LRW); 40 character symbols for open-vocabulary sentences
speaker: Not stated; GRID random split with overlapped speakers
mode: Voiced speech video; video only at test
key_result: WER 1.3% GRID, 16.3% LRW, 51.7% LRS2, 60.1% LRS3 (Table 3)
limitations: Single runs; LM use not stated; STFM compared only with global average pooling; Transformer baselines reproduced without MV-LRS

title: Speech Synthesis from ECoG using Densely Connected 3D Convolutional Neural Networks
authors: Miguel Angrick; Christian Herff; Emily Mugler; Matthew C. Tate; Marc W. Slutzky; Dean J. Krusienski; Tanja Schultz
summary: 3D DenseNet regressor (M06) and LJ-Speech WaveNet (M08) are standard: no in-paper baseline, mixed later head-to-heads, and no listener test behind the quality claims.
sensor: 64-ch 8x8 ECoG, 4 mm
task: Reconstruction of overt single words as audio (logMel spectrogram, WaveNet waveform)
vocabulary: Single-word reading, 244-372 words per participant; unique word count not stated
speaker: Six participants, models fit per participant
session: One awake-craniotomy recording per participant, 8.5-12.7 min
key_result: Per-participant mean spectrogram correlation r = 0.19-0.69 across six participants, above a retrained shuffle null (p < 0.001); STOI only plotted.
limitations: No baseline regressor or vocoder baseline; no listener or identification test; vocoder trained on another single speaker; fold unit, seeds and normalization scope not stated; offline.

title: Speech synthesis from neural decoding of spoken sentences
authors: Gopala K. Anumanchipalli; Josh Chartier; Edward F. Chang
summary: Two-stage bLSTM decoder maps ECoG during reading aloud to inferred articulatory features and then to acoustic parameters, synthesizing sentence waveforms (median MCD 5.14-6.58 dB in five participants). The two-stage model beat a direct decoder by 0.54 dB in P1, but the intermediate targets add phonetic-label supervision and the decoders differ in depth and learning rate; listener transcription used closed 25/50-word pools.
sensor: Clinical high-density ECoG (high gamma 70-200 Hz and 1-30 Hz)
task: Sentence-level speech synthesis from neural signals
vocabulary: Read sentences (MOCHA-TIMIT and others); closed 25/50-word pools for listener transcription
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: Median MCD 5.14-6.58 dB; 0.54 dB better than direct decoding (P1); listener median WER 31% (25-word pool) and 53% (50-word pool)
limitations: Decoder comparison and listener tests in P1 only, repetitions not stated; extra phonetic supervision in the intermediate stage (the authors tried a 6-layer direct decoder and kept the better 4-layer one); closed-pool transcription without chance level; mimed-speech values (58 trials of 10 sentences) in figures only, with inconsistent counts; read from the author manuscript (bioRxiv 2018-11 and published versions not compared).

title: Towards reconstructing intelligible speech from the human auditory cortex
authors: Hassan Akbari; Bahar Khalighinejad; Jose L. Herrero; Ashesh D. Mehta; Nima Mesgarani
summary: M06 ahead for heard speech: a pretrained autoencoder code of vocoder parameters beats spectrograms in all five patients; synthesizer decoding dates to 2009; M12 listener test unrepeated.
sensor: ECoG grids and depth electrodes; low-frequency plus high-gamma input
speaker: Not stated

title: Ultrasound-based Silent Speech Interface Built on a Continuous Vocoder
authors: Tamás Gábor Csapó; Mohammed Salah Al-Radhi; Géza Németh; Gábor Gosztolya; Tamás Grósz; László Tóth; Alexandra Markó
summary: Continuous F0 targets from articulation were prior work; MVF carrying voicing instead of a flag is new but unproven: the F0 RMSE gain uses different reference contours and naturalness is not better.
sensor: Midsagittal ultrasound tongue imaging (Micro system, 81.67 fps), one 64x128 frame per prediction
task: Ultrasound-to-speech synthesis with a continuous vocoder (continuous F0, maximum voiced frequency, MGC-LSP)
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: ContF0 RMSE 30.56 Hz vs 65.34 Hz for discontinuous F0, measured against different reference contours; MUSHRA naturalness 43.45 vs 40.87 with predicted excitation and original spectra, not significant; four speakers, 9 test sentences each
limitations: Continuous F0 targets from articulation were prior work; RMSE comparison not like-for-like and untested; no significant naturalness gain; no intelligibility test, no flag-plus-continuous-F0 control, no seeds; speaker-dependent, vocalized speech only; real-time claim unmeasured.

title: Video-Driven Speech Reconstruction using Generative Adversarial Networks
authors: Konstantinos Vougioukas; Pingchuan Ma; Stavros Petridis; Maja Pantic
summary: Direct-waveform GAN (M06) and speech-encoder perceptual loss (M02) are early but standard; the perceptual loss carries the words. Unseen-speaker WER 40.5% (successor 16%); no listener test.
sensor: Camera (silent frontal face video)
speaker: Both
key_result: Seen GRID speakers: ASR WER 26.6%, STOI 0.518 (Lip2AudSpec 32.5%, 0.446), PESQ 1.71 below Lip2AudSpec 1.82; without the perceptual loss WER 83.3%. Unseen speakers: WER 40.5%, STOI 0.445, PESQ 1.24.
limitations: GRID only, single runs, no listener test or chance level; a persistent hum lowers PESQ; unseen speakers get wrong-gender or morphing voices and 40% to 60% WER per speaker; the perceptual encoder's training speakers are unstated; frontal faces only.

title: AlterEgo: A Personalized Wearable Silent Speech Interface
venue: Proceedings of the 23rd International Conference on Intelligent User Interfaces (IUI '18), pp. 43-53
authors: Arnav Kapur; Shreyas Kapur; Pattie Maes
summary: Wearable headset that recognizes silently articulated words from face and jaw neuromuscular signals and answers through bone-conduction audio; abstract reports 92% median word accuracy in user studies.
sensor: Head-worn surface EMG electrodes on face and jaw, with bone-conduction headphones
vocabulary: Small task vocabularies (about 20 words per application, per MIT News)
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: 92% median word accuracy in user studies (abstract)
limitations: Small closed vocabularies and per-user customization; full protocol (splits, sessions, architecture) not verified because only the abstract and press coverage were available.

title: Audio-Visual Speech Recognition with a Hybrid CTC/Attention Architecture
authors: Stavros Petridis; Themos Stafylakis; Pingchuan Ma; Georgios Tzimiropoulos; Maja Pantic
summary: No earlier sentence-level AVSR study in the ledger trains hybrid CTC/attention (0 of 32), but no CTC- or attention-only result, LRW under the no-external-data claim, one run: standard.
sensor: Mouth ROI video and 83 audio features; early or late fusion
speaker: Thousands of BBC speakers; speaker overlap across splits not stated
key_result: 7.0% LRS2 audio-visual WER (early fusion) against 8.3% audio-only and 63.5% visual-only
limitations: One run; no CTC-only, attention-only or LM-free result; result partition not written next to Table 2

title: Decoding spoken phonemes from sensorimotor cortex with High-Density ECoG grids
authors: NF Ramsey; E Salari; EJ Aarnoutse; MJ Vansteensel; MG Bleichner; ZV Freudenburg
summary: Spatiotemporal templates on HD-ECoG (M06, M05) reuse the group's gesture decoder; the density claim is untested: standard. Voice-onset and rest anchoring confound the temporal gain.
sensor: HD-ECoG, 3–4 mm, 32–72 electrodes
task: Classification of overtly produced isolated phonemes and rest from sensorimotor HD-ECoG
speaker: Within-participant (5 epilepsy patients, Dutch)
session: Trial-level leave-one-out; runs and sessions not reported
key_result: STMF 75.5% five-class (empirical chance 26.4%), 71.9% four-phoneme (29.4%); SVM similar
limitations: Voice-onset and rest anchoring confound the temporal gain; no electrode-density test; no run- or session-held-out evaluation

title: Deep Audio-Visual Speech Recognition
authors: Triantafyllos Afouras; Joon Son Chung; Andrew Senior; Oriol Vinyals; Andrew Zisserman
summary: Landmark AVSR paper that releases LRS2-BBC and compares CTC and sequence-to-sequence Transformers on one shared encoder. Video-only TM-seq2seq reaches 48.3% WER with an LM (49.8% without; the 70.4% WAS baseline has no stated decoding conditions, and the same group's Transformer three months earlier already reached 50.0%). CTC and seq2seq differ little once an LM or audio is added.
sensor: Face/mouth video (25 fps, 112 px mouth crop) plus 16 kHz audio
task: Sentence-level lip reading and audio-visual speech recognition
speaker: Not stated
key_result: 48.3% WER video-only (LRS2-BBC, +LM); 8.2% audio-visual clean; 23.6% audio-visual in 0 dB babble
limitations: Test speakers may overlap with training (split by broadcast date, speaker count unreported); single runs; matched synthetic babble noise only; pretraining uses non-public MV-LRS; GPU model inconsistent between sections.

title: Deep Lip Reading: a comparison of models and an online application
authors: Triantafyllos Afouras; Joon Son Chung; Andrew Zisserman
summary: Standard: first CTC and Transformer lip readers side by side on LRS2, but objective and architecture are confounded and runs single; online decoding lacks partial-hypothesis accuracy and ms delay.
sensor: Mouth crop, 3D+ResNet front end
task: Open-vocabulary sentence-level visual speech recognition (lip reading) on LRS2
vocabulary: Open vocabulary; LRS2 training vocabulary over 40K words; character LSTM LM on T1 (2M words) or T2 (26M words)
speaker: BBC broadcast speakers; test-speaker overlap not stated
key_result: Transformer 50.0% WER on LRS2 test with T2 LM (51.2% with T1, 58.0% greedy); FC-15 55.0%; against a listed 70.4% baseline
limitations: One run per model; 70.4% baseline cited to two papers without conditions; MV-LRS and T2 not public; online decoding without measured delay or online error rate

title: Development of sEMG sensors and algorithms for silent speech recognition
authors: Geoffrey S. Meltzner; James T. Heaton; Yunbin Deng; Gianluca De Luca; Serge H. Roy; Joshua C. Kline
summary: Sensors, HMM decoder and class grammar are standard; the 8.9% WER is five of six subjects of the authors' uncited 2014 table (six-subject mean 11.2%).
sensor: Face- and neck-worn surface EMG sensors
speaker: Subject-dependent; 19 enrolled, 3 excluded, 5 tabulated for the final system
session: Single sessions of 4-6 h per subject; no cross-session test
key_result: 8.9% mean WER over five tabulated subjects on 1,200 continuous phrases from a 2,200-word corpus; the same system's 2014 six-subject mean is 11.2%, and the best 8 of 11 sensors give 10.4% WER.
limitations: Changed components are all standard; no stated test partition, seeds or validation set; subject-dependent models with 2-3 h training per user; one of six Corpus 3 subjects missing from Table 2 and not identified; comparisons with prior work use unmatched protocols.

title: End-to-End Audiovisual Speech Recognition
venue: IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech and Signal Processing (ICASSP)
authors: Stavros Petridis; Themos Stafylakis; Pingchuan Ma; Feipeng Cai; Georgios Tzimiropoulos; Maja Pantic
summary: Raw-waveform front end and BGRU fusion (M06) are standard: they tie MFCC in clean LRW audio (97.7%), and the noise gains rest on one run with the same babble noise in training and test.
sensor: 96x96 mouth crop; raw waveform
speaker: More than 1000 speakers (LRW); speaker overlap not stated
key_result: LRW: audio-visual 98.0%, raw-waveform audio 97.7%, MFCC audio 97.7%, visual 82.0%; +14.1 points over audio at -5 dB babble
limitations: No repeated runs or variance reported; same babble noise type and SNR range in training and test; MFCC baseline lacks the ResNet front end; no fusion alternative

title: Harnessing AI for Speech Reconstruction using Multi-view Silent Video Feed
venue: Proceedings of the 26th ACM International Conference on Multimedia (MM '18)
authors: Yaman Kumar; Mayank Aggarwal; Pratham Nawal; Shin'ichi Satoh; Rajiv Ratn Shah; Roger Zimmermann
summary: Multi-view input (M05) is new for video-to-speech but standard on its evidence: 2 speakers, gains overstated (11.4% in Table 1, 26% in text); PESQ only, no listener test (M12).
sensor: Two of five synchronized OuluVS2 camera views (0/30/45/60/90 deg)
task: Speech waveform reconstruction from multi-view silent video
vocabulary: OuluVS2 phrases, digit sequences and TIMIT sentences
speaker: Two reported speakers (1 and 10); training split not stated
key_result: PESQ 1.9683 / 1.9978 for 0+30 deg against 1.7674 / 1.7812 for 0 deg (Table 1)
limitations: Two speakers, no repeats or split stated, best pairs only, PESQ only with no listener test; every stated gain exceeds Table 1.

title: Inferring imagined speech using EEG signals: a new approach using Riemannian manifold features
authors: Chuong H. Nguyen; George K. Karavas; Panagiotis Artemiadis
summary: Tangent-space covariance + RVM (M06) is new to imagined-speech EEG but a cited motor-imagery pipeline; gains are not uniform and later grouped-CV work finds non-speech confounds.
sensor: 64-channel scalp EEG, 256 Hz, 8–70 Hz
task: Closed-set imagined-speech classification: 3 vowels, 3 short words, 2 long words, short versus long word
speaker: Within-subject; 15 healthy adults, 6-8 per task
session: 1-3 sessions per subject, randomized 10-fold CV within task
key_result: Mean accuracy 49.0% (3 vowels), 50.1% (3 short words), 66.2% (2 long words), 80.1% (short vs long, method 2)
limitations: Per-subject tuning without a stated selection set; no test against chance; visual cue present in the analysed interval; later grouped-CV re-analysis reports lower accuracy

title: Large-Scale Visual Speech Recognition
authors: Brendan Shillingford; Yannis Assael; Matthew W. Hoffman; Thomas Paine; Cían Hughes; Utsav Prabhu; Hank Liao; Hasim Sak; Kanishka Rao; Lorrayne Bennett; Marie Mulville; Ben Coppin; Ben Laurie; Andrew Senior; Nando de Freitas
summary: Its YouTube mining scaled on in later work, but Table 1 holds data fixed; the phoneme+WFST decoder had 2016-17 priors; zero-shot LRS3 changes everything at once: standard.
sensor: Mouth-region video, faces within 30 degrees
task: Open-vocabulary sentence-level visual speech recognition (lip reading) from YouTube video
vocabulary: 127,055-word corpus vocabulary; about 1M-word 5-gram LM at decoding
speaker: Thousands of YouTube speakers; split and overlap not stated
key_result: 40.9% WER on held-out LSVSR test; 55.1% WER zero-shot on full LRS3-TED test
limitations: Test split and speaker overlap not stated; LM corpus not named; one training run with bootstrap intervals; no data-size ablation
