title: LCANet: End-to-End Lipreading with Cascaded Attention-CTC
venue: IEEE International Conference on Automatic Face and Gesture Recognition (FG)
authors: Kai Xu; Dawei Li; Nick Cassimatis; Xiaolong Wang
summary: New attention-before-CTC decoder for lip reading, but one corpus, one run and no in-house CTC-only or attention-only baseline make it standard; against LRSW it is a tie.
sensor: RGB camera, 100x50 mouth crop
speaker: Not stated

title: Lip2AudSpec: Speech Reconstruction from Silent Lip Movements Video
venue: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech and Signal Processing (ICASSP)
authors: Hassan Akbari; Himani Arora; Liangliang Cao; Nima Mesgarani
summary: Bottleneck target (M02) and auditory-spectrogram route (M06) are standard; gains rest on one speaker, a re-implemented baseline and a vocabulary-cued test on four seen GRID speakers.
sensor: Camera (silent lip video)
task: Speech synthesis from silent lip video
speaker: Not stated
key_result: Human word accuracy 55.8% vs 50.9% baseline; STMI 0.80 vs 0.52, four GRID speakers
limitations: Only four GRID speakers and closed vocabulary; lip-only input misses tongue and throat cues; no real-world recordings.

title: Updating the Silent Speech Challenge benchmark with deep learning
authors: Yan Ji; Licheng Liu; Hongcui Wang; Zhilei Liu; Zhibin Niu; Bruce Denby
summary: Kaldi DNN-HMM cuts SSC WER from 17.4% to 6.45% (M06, M12: standard), but with the same bigram its own GMM gives 12.71%, so the DNN halves WER; one speaker, single runs.
sensor: Under-chin ultrasound transducer plus lip camera
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: 6.45% WER on the SSC test (Kaldi DNN-HMM, 30 DCT features, closed WSJ 5k bigram) vs the 17.4% benchmark; with the same bigram the paper's own triphone2b GMM-HMM gives 12.71%, and the less task-specific CSR 5k bigram gives 11.44%.
limitations: One speaker, 1023 test words, single runs without seeds or significance tests; only 5k-vocabulary WSJ0 bigram language models; the DAE advantage at 5 dimensions rests on DCT runs that fail (98-100% WER), a collapse the paper leaves unexplained.

title: Visual-Only Recognition of Normal, Whispered and Silent Speech
venue: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech and Signal Processing (ICASSP)
authors: Stavros Petridis; Jie Shen; Doruk Cetin; Maja Pantic
summary: Ahead on data: the first public three-mode lip-video corpus. Standard on transfer: the silent drop was known, and most of it is test-mode difficulty, not the training mode.
sensor: Video cameras, frontal view used (45-degree and profile recorded)
task: Closed-set visual-only utterance classification across normal, whispered and silent speech
speaker: Speaker-independent (digits 30/10/13, phrases 20/8/11 train/validation/test speakers)
key_result: Normal-trained: 68.0 to 59.7% (digits) and 69.7 to 61.2% (phrases) from normal to silent test; on the silent test, silent training gains only 2.5 and 3.2 points over normal training, and whispered training is best for silent phrases (65.1%).
limitations: Closed 10-class tasks; train-mode and test-mode effects not separated; no significance tests or chance level; seeds and stopping rule not stated; utterance boundaries still under correction at publication.

title: Biosignal-Based Spoken Communication: A Survey
venue: IEEE/ACM Transactions on Audio, Speech, and Language Processing 25(12), 2257-2271
authors: Tanja Schultz; Michael Wand; Thomas Hueber; Dean J. Krusienski; Christian Herff; Jonathan S. Brumberg
summary: Survey that frames silent speech within biosignal-based spoken communication, spanning articulatory, muscular and neural signals for communication devices, rehabilitation and speech science.
sensor: Articulatory, muscular and neural biosignal sensors (review)
speaker: Not stated
key_result: Not reported
limitations: Reviewed from the abstract only; a survey without a unified benchmark, so its detailed comparisons were not checked.

title: Combining Residual Networks with LSTMs for Lipreading
authors: Themos Stafylakis; Georgios Tzimiropoulos
summary: 3D-conv + ResNet + Bi-LSTM (M06), which became the field default, and per-step training (M03) are standard only for lack of run counts; 83.0% trails audio-supervised 93.2% today.
sensor: Video camera (broadcast TV video, grayscale mouth crop)
task: Word-level visual speech recognition (lip reading) on LRW
speaker: Many TV speakers; LRW splits by broadcast date, speaker overlap not stated
mode: Offline, visual only, no word boundaries
key_result: 83.0% top-1 word accuracy on the LRW test set (run count not reported)
limitations: No run count or dispersion; one dataset; state-of-the-art margin is a single cross-system comparison; no latency

title: EMG-to-Speech: Direct Generation of Speech from Facial Electromyographic Signals
venue: IEEE/ACM Transactions on Audio, Speech, and Language Processing
authors: Matthias Janke; Lorenz Diener
summary: Only new mapping work (M06) is a BLSTM and a 4-way ranking, standard; direct route (M08) inherited; no silent test (M04) or listener transcription (M12), behind; identity/mood retention unmeasured.
sensor: Facial surface EMG: 35-channel two-array setup and six single electrodes
task: Direct EMG-to-speech conversion (GMM, Unit Selection, DNN, BLSTM) with MLSA vocoding
vocabulary: Read English broadcast-news, Arctic and TIMIT sentences; ASR evaluation at 108, 905 and 2,111 words
speaker: Three speakers, session-dependent models
key_result: Mean evaluation MCD 5.21 (DNN) vs 5.69 (GMM); DNN mapping under 0.1 real time
limitations: No silent-articulation test; no listener transcription; 10-20 evaluation utterances per session

title: High performance communication by people with paralysis using an intracortical brain-computer interface
authors: Chethan Pandarinath; Paul Nuyujukian; Christine H. Blabe; Brittany L. Sorice; Jad Saab; Francis R. Willett; Leigh R. Hochberg; Krishna V. Shenoy; Jaimie M. Henderson
summary: ReFIT-KF + HMM click (M06) and ccpm/bitrate protocol (M12) are standard for 2017; 1.4-4.2x record gains are cross-study and the HMM is never isolated; later decoders reach 110 chars/min.
sensor: 96-ch arrays; spikes, HF-LFP (T6)
speaker: Not stated

title: Improved Speech Reconstruction from Silent Video
venue: 2017 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision Workshops (ICCVW)
authors: Ariel Ephrat; Tavi Halperin; Shmuel Peleg
summary: Optical-flow tower (M05) and mel-to-linear post-net (M06) are standard: no flow gain in Table 5; trails Le Cornu on S3; no listener test (M12); Lip2Wav's re-run: 27.83% vs 14.08% WER.
sensor: Camera (full-face video plus optical flow)
vocabulary: 51-word GRID grammar plus unseen words in TCD-TIMIT
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: GRID S4 STOI 0.700 vs 0.584 for Vid2speech, but behind Le Cornu and Milner on S3 ESTOI (0.398 vs 0.437) and PESQ; in Lip2Wav's re-run of the method, 27.83% GRID WER vs 14.08% for Lip2Wav
limitations: Speaker-dependent; objective metrics only, no listener or ASR test; single splits without seeds or intervals; optical-flow tower shows no gain in its ablation; post-net gain comes from a row mixing two synthesis paths; TCD-TIMIT result holds for one of three speakers.

title: Lip Reading Sentences in the Wild
authors: Joon Son Chung; Andrew Senior; Oriol Vinyals; Andrew Zisserman
summary: Introduces Watch, Listen, Attend and Spell and the BBC LRS dataset. Lips-only decoding reaches 50.2% WER on open-vocabulary broadcast sentences against 73.8% for a professional lipreader, but the lipreader worked on 200 clips under different viewing conditions with declined clips excluded (87.6% with them), and the machine score is not stated to be on the same clips. The word-to-sentence curriculum gives the largest single gain (76.5% to 61.1%), from one training run.
sensor: Camera (broadcast mouth crops, 120 px grey, 25 Hz), optional audio (13-dim MFCC)
task: Sentence-level lip reading and audio-visual speech recognition
speaker: Not stated
key_result: 50.2% lips-only WER on LRS (professional lipreader 73.8% on 200 clips); 13.9% audio-visual WER clean vs 17.7% audio-only; 3.0% WER on GRID (overlapped-speaker split)
limitations: Train/test speaker overlap unreported (date split only); single runs; human comparison under unequal conditions; noise type at test unstated; LRS was never released.

title: Seeing Through Noise: Visually Driven Speaker Separation and Enhancement
authors: Aviv Gabbay; Ariel Ephrat; Tavi Halperin; Shmuel Peleg
summary: Uses visual speech predictions from face video to build masks that separate or enhance a target speaker from audio mixtures, beating audio-only separation on GRID and TCD-TIMIT. Not an SSI paper.
sensor: Camera plus microphone (face video and audio)
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: GRID separation SDR 5.62, PESQ 2.6 vs audio-only 1.74, 1.85
limitations: Not SSI; speaker-dependent models, unknown speakers need fine-tuning, and evaluation uses synthetic two-speaker mixtures.

title: Vid2speech: Speech Reconstruction from Silent Video
venue: 2017 IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech and Signal Processing (ICASSP)
authors: Ariel Ephrat; Shmuel Peleg
summary: Raw-face CNN to LSP (M05, M06) is standard: 82.6% vs 40.0% over Le Cornu and Milner mixes in forced-choice listening (M12); as a whole system it later scores 44.92% vs 14.08% GRID WER (Lip2Wav).
sensor: Camera (GRID face video, 25 fps)
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: 82.6% audio-only intelligibility (S4) vs 40.0% prior work; OOV 51.6% vs 10% chance
limitations: Speaker-specific training, constrained GRID grammar, unnatural-sounding resynthesis, and a small listening study without open-vocabulary or live testing.

title: Contour-based 3d tongue motion visualization using ultrasound image sequences
authors: Kele Xu; Yin Yang; Clemence Leboullenger; Pierre Roussel; Bruce Denby
summary: Builds a contour-based pipeline that maps midsagittal ultrasound tongue contours to 3D tongue motion using a database of 1000 3D shapes; evaluation is qualitative, with about 1.2 s per frame association.
sensor: B-mode ultrasound tongue imaging
speaker: Not stated
key_result: Not reported (about 1.2 s average to associate a frame with the 3D model)
limitations: Not a recognizer; uses only midsagittal information with a simplified driving scheme and has no quantitative accuracy benchmark.

title: Fully Implanted Brain-Computer Interface in a Locked-In Patient with ALS
authors: Mariska J. Vansteensel; Elmar G. M. Pels; Martin G. Bleichner; Mariana P. Branco; Timothy Denison; Zachary V. Freudenburg; Peter Gosselaar; Sacha Leinders; Thomas H. Ottens; Max A. Van Den Boom; Peter C. Van Rijen; Erik J. Aarnoutse; Nick F. Ramsey
summary: Skin-closed ECoG implant used at home without investigators (M13): standard, one user, skin-closed telemetry predates it; main-text 89% spelling accuracy pools inactive steps, no chance level.
sensor: Subdural ECoG strips with a fully implanted amplifier and transmitter
task: Letter selection by attempted-hand-movement brain clicks in a scanning speller
speaker: One participant with late-stage ALS
session: 67 home sessions over 262 days; independent home use from day 197
key_result: 89% spelling accuracy (active and inactive steps pooled); about two letters per minute with word prediction
limitations: One participant; no chance level or false-click rate; set-up assistance needed

title: LipNet: End-to-End Sentence-level Lipreading
authors: Yannis M. Assael; Brendan Shillingford; Shimon Whiteson; Nando de Freitas
summary: A new CTC sentence decoder, but one corpus and one run make it standard; the comparisons break: an 86.4% word-level HMM baseline, a 10-minute panel, silent dictation untested.
sensor: Camera (frontal face/lip video)
speaker: Both
key_result: 4.8% WER overlapped speakers, 11.4% WER unseen speakers on GRID
limitations: Only GRID's tiny fixed grammar with vocalized speech; no open vocabulary, in-the-wild, silent-articulation or real-time evaluation.

title: Lipreading with Long Short-Term Memory
venue: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech and Signal Processing (ICASSP)
authors: Michael Wand; Jan Koutník; Jürgen Schmidhuber
summary: Joint LSTM + pixel front end (M06) is ahead of 2015 lipreading, but pixel-input and recurrent word models predate it, and the 8.3-point gain is over linear SVMs, not HMMs.
sensor: Existing GRID video, 40 x 40 grayscale mouth crop; no new sensor
task: Visual-only word classification from lip video
speaker: Speaker-dependent, 19 speakers (1-9 development, 10-19 evaluation)
key_result: Word accuracy 79.6% (SD 4.3%) on evaluation speakers 10-19 against 71.3% for HOG + SVM and 70.6% for Eigenlips + SVM (Table 1).
limitations: Pixel-input neural lipreading predates it (1994 MS-TDNN, uncited); baselines are linear SVMs without an HMM; word clips cut from corpus alignments; speaker-dependent random splits; seeds and t-test details not stated.

title: Neural speech recognition: continuous phoneme decoding using spatiotemporal representations of human cortical activity
authors: David A. Moses; Nima Mesgarani; Matthew K. Leonard; Edward F. Chang
summary: ASR decoding (M06) and phoneme LM (M07) on heard-speech ECoG: standard, with ECoG precedents of 2015. Electrodes chosen on the test set (M12); LM effect not isolated from smoothing.
sensor: 256-electrode subdural ECoG, 70-150 Hz high gamma
task: Continuous phoneme decoding from heard speech (TIMIT, reenacted film dialogue)
vocabulary: 39 phoneme classes; phoneme 4-gram LM, no word lexicon
speaker: Three listeners; two Gump test speakers, 402 TIMIT speakers
session: Within-session stimulus-level 10-fold cross-validation; session count not stated
key_result: Decoding PER 70.47% with averaged, pooled responses of three subjects; 85.71-90.63% single-trial single-subject; chance 97.12% (Table 5)
limitations: Electrodes selected on the evaluation set; LM effect not isolated from HMM smoothing; two test speakers

title: Word pair classification during imagined speech using direct brain recordings
authors: Stephanie Martin; Peter Brunner; Iñaki Iturrate; José del R. Millán; Gerwin Schalk; Robert T. Knight; Brian N. Pasley
summary: Whole-word output (M08) is new only to intracranial recordings (Suppes 1997, EEG/MEG); DTW kernel (M06) gain unshown; imagery window confounded by heard and upcoming overt word.
sensor: Clinical ECoG, 5 patients, high gamma 70-150 Hz
task: Binary classification of imagined, heard and overt word pairs
speaker: 5 epilepsy patients
key_result: Imagined mean 57.7% (chance 50%), significant in 4 of 5 subjects
limitations: Offline, binary, cue-locked imagined epochs, no same-delay no-imagery control

title: Audio-visual speech recognition using deep learning
authors: Kuniaki Noda; Yuki Yamaguchi; Kazuhiro Nakadai; Hiroshi G. Okuno; Tetsuya Ogata
summary: Both front ends are new to their 2014 populations but transfer outside designs without repetition (M06 standard); stream weights and depth are tuned on the test words (M12 behind).
sensor: One frontal monochrome camera, one microphone
speaker: Not stated

title: Brain-to-text: decoding spoken phrases from phone representations in the brain
authors: Christian Herff; Dominic Heger; Adriana de Pesters; Dominic Telaar; Peter Brunner; Gerwin Schalk; Tanja Schultz
summary: Phone-model decoder (M06) is the EMG recognizer moved to ECoG: standard. 25% WER uses per-phrase dictionaries holding the spoken words (M07); the time-shift null (M12) is sound.
sensor: ECoG grids, 70-170 Hz log power
task: Offline decoding of overt read-aloud phrases into words from ECoG
vocabulary: Phrase-specific dictionaries containing the spoken words plus random words (10 words and larger)
speaker: 7 epilepsy patients, per-session models
key_result: WER as low as 25% and phone error below 50% (Abstract); 75% of words correct with a 10-word dictionary (Sec. 3.2)
limitations: Dictionaries always contain the spoken words; LM estimated on the read texts with no stated exclusion of the test phrase; no cross-session test; offline only

title: Decoding spectrotemporal features of overt and covert speech from the human cortex
authors: Stéphanie Martin; Peter Brunner; Chris Holdgraf; Hans-Jochen Heinze; Nathan E. Crone; Jochem Rieger; Gerwin Schalk; Robert T. Knight; Brian N. Pasley
summary: Overt-trained ECoG decoding of covert reading (M04), spectral outputs (M08) and the overt-recording covert reference (M11) are standard; DTW-aligned rest reaches r 0.30 vs covert 0.34.
sensor: Clinical ECoG, high gamma
task: Offline reconstruction of auditory spectrogram and modulation features from ECoG during overt and covert reading of continuous text
vocabulary: Continuous text (political speeches, a children story)
speaker: 7 epilepsy patients, within-subject
session: Single clinical monitoring period; random 90/10 split of 7-s blocks
mode: Overt and covert (silent) reading; resting control
key_result: Overt identification rank 0.91; covert spectrogram r 0.34 vs DTW-aligned rest 0.30; covert rank 0.55
limitations: Covert effect small against warped baseline; no held-out story or seeds; no audio rendering

title: Direct classification of all American English phonemes using signals from functional speech motor cortex
authors: Emily M Mugler; James L Patton; Robert D Flint; Zachary A Wright; Stephan U Schuele; Joshua Rosenow; Jerry J Shih; Dean J Krusienski; Marc W Slutzky
summary: Phoneme-onset events within words (M06) are ahead as a protocol; full-inventory classification predates it (Brumberg 2011); the 36% headline is consonants only, on hand-labelled onsets.
sensor: Clinical ECoG grids, high-gamma, mu, beta, LMP
task: Overt reading of prompted monosyllabic words; phoneme classification
vocabulary: 320 words (Modified Rhyme Test plus 20), General American phoneme inventory
speaker: 4 epilepsy patients, within-subject
key_result: 20.4% mean all-phoneme accuracy vs 7.4% shuffled chance; 36.1% consonants in best subject
limitations: Hand-labelled acoustic onsets at test; vowels and consonants analysed separately; selection nesting not stated

title: Lipreading using Convolutional Neural Network
authors: Kuniaki Noda; Yuki Yamaguchi; Kazuhiro Nakadai; Hiroshi G. Okuno; Tetsuya Ogata
summary: New 2-D CNN front end (0 of 110 prior decoders) but an unrepeated gain (M06 standard); test-word frames trained the CNN, inflating its PCA comparison (M12 behind).
sensor: One frontal 100 Hz monochrome camera; manual mouth crop
task: Visual-only isolated Japanese word recognition via CNN phoneme posteriors
speaker: Six male speakers; speaker-dependent CNNs; seen-speaker word test
key_result: Mean phoneme rate 58% (40 classes, shuffled frames); best word rate about 37% (84 test words unseen by the HMM, seen speakers)
limitations: Test-word frames in CNN training; supervised CNN against unsupervised baselines; no repeated runs or significance test

title: Reconstructing Speech from Human Auditory Cortex
authors: Brian N. Pasley; Stephen V. David; Nima Mesgarani; Adeen Flinker; Shihab A. Shamma; Nathan E. Crone; Robert T. Knight; Edward F. Chang
summary: M06 ahead for 2012: earliest heard-speech spectrogram reconstruction from human ECoG in the ledger, above zero in all 15 patients; modulation result is a group effect; word readout uses one patient.
sensor: Subdural ECoG, 4 or 10 mm grids, high gamma
task: Reconstruction of heard speech (auditory spectrogram and temporal-modulation energy) from STG high-gamma, plus closed-set word identification
vocabulary: Isolated words and pseudowords from one speaker (10 participants), TIMIT sentences (5); identification among 47 candidates
speaker: 15 neurosurgical patients (epilepsy or tumor); one for word identification
session: Within-participant random trial subsampling and leave-one-word-out cross-validation; sessions not stated
key_result: Mean single-trial spectrogram reconstruction r = 0.28; nonlinear modulation model better at fast rates (F(1,14) = 33.36); median word-identification rank 0.76 single trial, 0.89 averaged (chance 0.5)
limitations: Word identification in one participant from one speaker's 47 items; no listener intelligibility test; no noise-ceiling correction; tasks and stimulus sets pooled; offline only

title: Classification of intended phoneme production from chronic intracortical microelectrode recordings in speech-motor cortex
authors: Jonathan S. Brumberg; E. Joe Wright; Dinal S. Andreasen; Frank H. Guenther; Philip R. Kennedy
summary: 38-phoneme intracortical classification (M06) is standard: isolated-phoneme sets preceded it in EMG, one participant, no repetition; bins, not trials, were split into folds.
sensor: Neurotrophic Electrode, 2 channels, 31 clusters
task: Off-line 38-class classification of attempted isolated English phonemes
speaker: One locked-in participant
session: Five sessions pooled; random 10-fold split over 300-ms bins
key_result: 16.9-21.0% overall accuracy against 2.6% chance (LDA/FDA/SVM)
limitations: Single participant; bins of a trial not stated to share a fold; no shuffled or rest control; attempt verified only post-trial; off-line only

title: Decoding Vowels and Consonants in Spoken and Imagined Words Using Electrocorticographic Signals in Humans
authors: Xiaomei Pei; Dennis Barbour; Eric C. Leuthardt; Gerwin Schalk
summary: Paired covert/overt vowel and consonant-class decoding on ECoG (M04) is ahead as a 2011 protocol; best-of-47–64-electrode selection and prompt-only covert labels make its gains upper bounds.
sensor: Clinical grids, 48 or 64 contacts
task: Four-class vowel and consonant-pair classification from overt and covert (imagined) repetition of 36 monosyllabic words
vocabulary: Closed set: 36 CVC words, 4 vowels, 9 consonant pairs
speaker: 8 epilepsy patients (overt), 6 of them covert
key_result: Best-electrode accuracy 40.7% overt and 37.5% covert for vowels, 40.6% and 36.3% for consonant pairs (25% chance)
limitations: Best of 47-64 electrodes; fold nesting of feature and electrode selection not stated; covert labels taken from the prompt; offline only

title: Using the electrocorticographic speech network to control a brain-computer interface in humans
authors: Eric C. Leuthardt; Charles Gaona; Mohit Sharma; Nicholas Szrama; Jarod Roland; Zac Freudenberg; Jamie Solis; Jonathan Breshears; Gerwin Schalk
summary: Speech-task ECoG cursor control (M04) and 1-mm microgrid control (M05) are standard: closed-loop speech-cortex and word-task ECoG BCIs preceded it; imagined vowel pairs were never tested.
sensor: 10-mm grids; one 1-mm microgrid
task: Closed-loop 1-D cursor control from cued overt or imagined vowels
vocabulary: Two choices (vowel vs vowel or vowel vs rest)
speaker: Four epilepsy patients, per-patient features
session: Single screening and control run per patient
key_result: Final accuracy 68-91% (noise floor 46.2%) over 61-139 trials
limitations: Condition confounded with patient; imagined pairs untested; Table 2 and Fig. 8 disagree

title: Decoding spoken words using local field potentials recorded from the cortical surface
authors: Spencer Kellis; Kai Miller; Kyle Thomson; Richard Brown; Paul House; Bradley Greger
summary: Micro-ECoG closed-set word decoding (M05, M06) departs from 2009 intracortical formant decoding and clinical grids but stays standard: one patient, one split, selection on test data.
sensor: Micro-ECoG, 2×16, 1 mm
speaker: Not stated

title: Development of a Silent Speech Interface Driven by Ultrasound and Optical Images of the Tongue and Lips
authors: Thomas Hueber; Elie-Laurent Benaroya; Gérard Chollet; Bruce Denby; Gérard Dreyfus; Maureen Stone
summary: HMM phone recognizer (M06) standard; recognition-then-unit-selection output (M08) departs from frame-wise mapping, incl. the group's 2007 one, but is tested only on oracle phones.
sensor: Ultrasound tongue imaging plus frontal and profile lip video
task: Continuous phone recognition and corpus-based speech synthesis
vocabulary: CMU-Arctic sentences; word dictionary of 2,569 items
speaker: Two speakers, speaker-dependent
key_result: Visual phone accuracy 59.0-67.6% (speaker A) and 48.3-56.0% (speaker B); synthesis tested on oracle phones
limitations: No silent-speech test; synthesis not evaluated from recognized phones

title: Modeling Coarticulation in EMG-based Continuous Speech Recognition
authors: Tanja Schultz; Michael Wand
summary: Bundled phonetic-feature streams (M06) are new among non-acoustic recognizers but transfer acoustic-ASR clustering; test-set tuning inflates the gain; speaker-independent and silent claims untested.
sensor: Five-channel facial surface EMG (Varioport, 600 Hz)
task: Continuous word recognition from EMG with bundled phonetic-feature streams
speaker: 14 pilot speakers; speaker-dependent and pooled multi-speaker models
mode: Audible read speech scored; silent speech recorded but not scored
key_result: Average WER 47.15% (phone baseline) to 31.49% (context-dependent bundled phonetic features), speaker-dependent
limitations: Stream weights and tree size tuned on the test set; no held-out speaker; no silent-speech score

title: Silent speech interfaces
authors: Bruce Denby; Tanja Schultz; Kiyoshi Honda; Thomas Hueber; James M. Gilbert; Jonathan S. Brumberg
summary: Founding review that defines silent speech interfaces, surveys seven sensing technologies from EMA to intracortical implants, and scores them on six practical criteria; concludes no technology meets all of them.
sensor: Seven SSI technology families (review)
speaker: Not stated
key_result: Not reported
limitations: Pre-deep-learning review; cited results are small-vocabulary and heterogeneous, and the comparison scores are qualitative.

title: A Wireless Brain-Machine Interface for Real-Time Speech Synthesis
authors: Frank H. Guenther; Jonathan S. Brumberg; E. Joseph Wright; Alfonso Nieto-Castanon; Jason A. Tourville; Mikhail Panko; Robert Law; Steven A. Siebert; Jess L. Bartels; Dinal S. Andreasen; Princewill Ehirim; Hui Mao; Philip R. Kennedy
summary: Closed-loop formant decoding (M06) and F1/F2 output (M08) are standard: gesture-driven formant synthesis came first; one user learns vowels; hit rate lacks a chance level; no speech measured.
sensor: Two-channel Neurotrophic Electrode, left precentral gyrus, transcutaneous FM telemetry
task: Real-time formant (F1/F2) synthesis of vowels in a center-out task
vocabulary: Three target vowels (IY, A, OO); four vowels in decoder training
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: Hit rate 45% to 70% and endpoint error 435 Hz to 233 Hz from first to last block, averaged across 25 sessions
limitations: One participant; vowels only; no chance level, decoder-off control or listener test; attractor force in target regions

title: Non-Audible Murmur (NAM) Recognition
venue: IEICE Transactions on Information and Systems
authors: Yoshitaka Nakajima; Hideki Kashioka; Nick Campbell; Kiyohiro Shikano
summary: Sensor, murmur mode and HMM retraining (M05, M04, M03) are the authors' 2003 design, standard for lack of repetition; noise robustness lacks levels and an air baseline.
sensor: Stethoscopic microphone below the mastoid
task: Large-vocabulary continuous dictation of non-audible murmur (Japanese, 20K words)
speaker: One male speaker, speaker-dependent
session: Not stated (training and test sessions not described)
key_result: 93.3% word accuracy in quiet, 88.4-90.0% in three everyday-noise rooms of unstated level, 24 sentences each (Table 1)
limitations: One speaker; rows A-C identical to the 2003 report; no noise levels or air-microphone baseline; test-text overlap with training not stated
